sentences.zh: 房琯，字次律，河南河南人。

translations.literal: Fang Guan, styled Cilü, was a native of Henan in Henan [commandery].
translations.idiomatic: Fang Guan, whose courtesy name was Cilü, came from Henan in Henan commandery.

sentences.zh: 父融，武后時，以正諫大夫同鳳閣鸞臺平章事；

translations.literal: His father Rong, during Empress Wu's reign, served as Remonstrating Grand Master and Associate Director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Phoenix Terrace Chancellery;
translations.idiomatic: His father Rong had served under Empress Wu as Remonstrating Grand Master and associate director of the Phoenix Pavilion and Phoenix Terrace chancellery;

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，貶死高州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong he was demoted and died at Gaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 705 he was banished and died in exile at Gaozhou.

sentences.zh: 琯少好學，風度沈整，以廕補弘文生。

translations.literal: Guan in his youth loved learning; his bearing was grave and composed; through yin privilege he was enrolled as a Hongwen student.
translations.idiomatic: Guan had loved scholarship from boyhood, carried himself with grave composure, and entered the Hongwen Academy by hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 與呂向偕隱陸渾山，十年不諧際人事。

translations.literal: With Lü Xiang he retired together to Mount Lu Hun; for ten years he did not engage with worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He and Lü Xiang withdrew together to Mount Lu Hun and for ten years kept out of public life entirely.

sentences.zh: 開元中，作《封禪書》，說宰相張說，說奇之，奏為校書郎。

translations.literal: During Kaiyuan he composed the Fengshan shu, presented it to Chancellor Zhang Yue; Yue marveled at it and memorialized him as collating editor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan era he wrote a treatise on the Feng and Shan sacrifices and showed it to Chancellor Zhang Yue, who was so impressed that he had Guan appointed collating editor.

sentences.zh: 舉任縣令科，授盧氏令。

translations.literal: He passed the special examination for county magistrates and was appointed magistrate of Lushi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the special examination for county magistrates and was made magistrate of Lushi.

sentences.zh: 拜監察御史，坐訊獄非是，貶睦州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor; for errors in conducting an interrogation he was demoted to revenue registrar of Muzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed investigating censor, he was later demoted to revenue registrar of Muzhou for irregularities in a trial he conducted.

sentences.zh: 復為縣，所至上德化，興長利，以治最顯。

translations.literal: Again he served as county magistrate; wherever he went he promoted virtue and transformation, developed lasting benefits, and became distinguished for the excellence of his governance.
translations.idiomatic: Restored to county office, he governed wherever he was posted with moral suasion, fostered lasting public benefit, and won renown for outstanding administration.

sentences.zh: 天寶五載，試給事中，封漳南縣男。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianbao he was tested as imperial attendant and enfeoffed as Baron of Zhangnan county.
translations.idiomatic: In 746 he was tried out as imperial attendant and enfeoffed as Baron of Zhangnan.

sentences.zh: 時玄宗有逸志，數巡幸，廣溫泉為華清宮，環宮所置百司區署。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xuanzong had wayward ambitions, made frequent tours, expanded the hot springs into Huaqing Palace, and set up the bureaus and offices around the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then indulged a taste for pleasure, traveled often, expanded the hot springs into Huaqing Palace, and grouped government offices around it.

sentences.zh: 以琯資機算，詔總經度驪山，疏岩剔藪，為天子游觀。

translations.literal: Because Guan possessed resourcefulness and calculation, he was ordered to oversee the works at Mount Li, clearing rocks and thinning thickets for the Son of Heaven's sightseeing.
translations.idiomatic: Deeming Guan clever and practical, the court put him in charge of developing Mount Li—clearing cliffs and thinning forests for the emperor's excursions.

sentences.zh: 未畢，坐善李適之、韋堅，斥為宜春太守。

translations.literal: Before the work was finished, for favoring Li Shizhi and Wei Jian he was dismissed as prefect of Yichun.
translations.idiomatic: Before the project was done, his association with Li Shizhi and Wei Jian cost him the post; he was sent out as prefect of Yichun.

sentences.zh: 曆琅邪、鄴、扶風三郡，頻遷憲部侍郎。

translations.literal: He successively held the three prefectures of Langye, Ye, and Fufeng, and was frequently promoted to vice minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as prefect of Langye, Ye, and Fufeng, and rose repeatedly until he became vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 十五載，帝狩蜀，琯馳至普安上謁，帝喜甚，即拜文部尚書、同中書門下平章事，從至成都，賜一子官。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the emperor hunted in Shu; Guan galloped to Pu'an to present himself; the emperor was greatly pleased and immediately appointed him Minister of Rites and co-chancellor; he followed to Chengdu and one son was granted an office.
translations.idiomatic: In 756, when the emperor fled into Shu, Guan rushed to Pu'an to pay homage. Delighted, the emperor at once made him Minister of Rites and co-chancellor, took him on to Chengdu, and granted an office to one of his sons.

sentences.zh: 俄與韋見素、崔渙奉冊靈武，見肅宗，具言上皇所以傳付意，因道當時利病，箝索虜情，辭吐華暢，帝為改容。

translations.literal: Soon with Wei Jiansu and Cui Huan he bore the registers to Lingwu, met Emperor Suzong, fully explained the Retired Emperor's intent in the transmission, and thereupon set forth the advantages and harms of the time, enumerating the enemy's situation; his words flowed with brilliance and ease, and the emperor changed expression.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he went with Wei Jiansu and Cui Huan to Lingwu to present the imperial register to Suzong, explained Xuanzong's purpose in abdicating, analyzed current strengths and weaknesses, and laid out the rebels' position in flowing, eloquent speech that made the emperor sit up.

sentences.zh: 琯既有重名。

translations.literal: Guan already had a great reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Guan already enjoyed great fame.

sentences.zh: 帝傾意待之，機務一二與琯參決，諸將相莫敢望。

translations.literal: The emperor poured out his favor on him; one or two matters of state he decided together with Guan; none of the generals or chancellors dared compare.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor leaned on him wholeheartedly, consulted him on crucial affairs, and none of the other generals or ministers could rival his standing.

sentences.zh: 於是，第五琦言財利幸，為江淮租庸使。

translations.literal: Thereupon Diwu Qi, speaking of finance and profit, won favor and became Jiang-Huai commissioner for tax and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: At this point Diwu Qi, who traded on expertise in finance, won favor and was made commissioner for Jiang-Huai tax and corvée.

sentences.zh: 琯諫曰：「往楊國忠聚斂，產怨天下。

translations.literal: Guan remonstrated, saying: "Formerly Yang Guozhong amassed exactions and produced resentment throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Guan remonstrated: "Under Yang Guozhong the court squeezed revenue until the empire seethed with resentment.

sentences.zh: 陛下即位，人未見德，今又寵琦，是一國忠死，一國忠生，無以示遠方。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty has ascended the throne but the people have not yet seen virtue; now You again favor Qi—it is one Guozhong dead and another Guozhong born, with no way to show the distant regions.
translations.idiomatic: You have just taken the throne and the people have yet to see benevolent rule; if you favor Qi now, it will look as though one Guozhong has died only for another to rise—how can that reassure the provinces?

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「六軍之命方急，無財則散。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The Six Armies' fate is urgently at stake; without funds they will disperse.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "The armies' survival hangs in the balance; without money they will scatter.

sentences.zh: 卿惡琦可也，何所取財？」

translations.literal: You may hate Qi, but where will wealth be taken from?"
translations.idiomatic: You may dislike Qi as you please, but where else will the funds come from?

sentences.zh: 琯不得對。

translations.literal: Guan could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Guan had no answer.

sentences.zh: 北海太守賀蘭進明自河南至，詔攝御史大夫、嶺南節度使，入謝，帝曰：「朕語琯除正大夫，何為攝邪？」

translations.literal: Beihai prefect Helan Jinming came from Henan; he was ordered as acting censor-in-chief and Lingnan military commissioner; entering to give thanks, the emperor said: "We told Guan to appoint you full grand master—why 'acting'?
translations.idiomatic: Helan Jinming, prefect of Beihai, arrived from Henan and was ordered to serve as acting censor-in-chief and military commissioner of Lingnan. When he came to give thanks, the emperor said, "I told Guan to appoint you full censor-in-chief—why 'acting'?

sentences.zh: 進明銜之，因曰：「陛下知晉亂乎？

translations.literal: Jinming bore a grudge over this and thereupon said: "Does Your Majesty know how Jin fell into disorder?
translations.idiomatic: Jinming took offense and said, "Does Your Majesty know how the Jin dynasty was ruined?

sentences.zh: 惟以尚虛名，任王衍為宰相，基祖浮華，不事天下事，故至於敗。

translations.literal: It was solely because they valued empty reputation, employed Wang Yan as chancellor, who founded his lineage in frivolity and ornament and did not attend to the realm's affairs, and therefore came to defeat.
translations.idiomatic: They prized empty reputation, put Wang Yan in the chancellery, and built policy on showy refinement while neglecting the realm—until the state collapsed.

sentences.zh: 方唐中興，當用實才，而琯性疏闊，大言無當，非宰相器。

translations.literal: Now as Tang is reviving, solid talent should be employed; yet Guan's nature is broad and loose, his grand words ineffectual—he is not material for chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Tang is trying to revive itself and needs practical men, but Guan is scatterbrained, full of empty talk, and unfit for the chancellery.

sentences.zh: 陛下待之厚，然孰肯為陛下用乎？」

translations.literal: Your Majesty treats him generously, yet who would be willing to serve Your Majesty for his sake?"
translations.idiomatic: You treat him generously, but who under him would truly serve you?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「何哉？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "How so?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "How so?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下頃為皇太子，太子出曰撫軍，入曰監國，而琯為聖皇建遣諸王為都統節度，乃謂陛下為元子而付以朔方、河東、河北空虛之地，永王、豐王乃統四節度。

translations.literal: He replied: "When Your Majesty was still crown prince, the prince going out was styled 'military governor' and coming in 'regent of the realm,' yet Guan, for the Retired Emperor, devised sending the princes as overall commanders and military commissioners, and thereby treated Your Majesty as eldest son while assigning You the empty territories of Shuofang, Hedong, and Hebei, while Prince Yong and Prince Feng commanded four military commissions.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "When you were crown prince, a prince leaving court was styled 'military overseer' and returning 'regent of the realm.' Yet Guan, acting for the retired emperor, had the princes made overall commanders and military commissioners: he treated you as eldest son but gave you the depleted territories of Shuofang, Hedong, and Hebei, while Princes Yong and Feng held four military commissions between them.

sentences.zh: 此於聖皇似忠，于陛下非忠也。

translations.literal: This toward the Retired Emperor seems loyal, but toward Your Majesty it is not loyal.
translations.idiomatic: That looked loyal to the retired emperor but was not loyal to you.

sentences.zh: 琯意諸子一得天下，身不失恩，又多樹私黨，以副戎權，推此而言，豈肯盡誠于陛下乎？」

translations.literal: Guan's intent was that whichever son gained the realm, he himself would not lose favor; moreover he planted many private factions to support military power—pursuing this reasoning, how could he be willing to devote full loyalty to Your Majesty?"
translations.idiomatic: Guan meant that whichever prince won the throne, he would keep his own favor; he also built private factions to back military power. On that logic, would he ever serve you with whole-hearted loyalty?"

sentences.zh: 帝入其語，始惡琯。

translations.literal: The emperor took in his words and began to dislike Guan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this account and began to turn against Guan.

sentences.zh: 以進明為御史大夫、河南節度使。

translations.literal: Jinming was appointed censor-in-chief and Henan military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Jinming was made censor-in-chief and military commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 會琯請自將平賊，帝猶倚以成功，乃詔琯持節招討西京、防禦蒲潼兩關兵馬節度等使，得自擇參佐。

translations.literal: When Guan requested to lead the troops himself to pacify the rebels, the emperor still relied on him for success and thereupon ordered Guan as commissioner with full powers to recruit and pacify the Western Capital, defend the Pu and Tong passes, and serve as military commissioner over the armies, with liberty to choose his own staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan asked to command the campaign himself, the emperor still hoped he would succeed and appointed him commissioner to recover the Western Capital, defend the Pu and Tong passes, and take overall command of the armies, with freedom to choose his own staff.

sentences.zh: 乃以兵部尚書王思禮、御史中丞鄧景山為副，戶部侍郎李揖為行軍司馬，中丞宋若思、起居郎知制誥賈至、右司郎中魏少游為判官，給事中劉秩為參謀。

translations.literal: Thereupon Minister of War Wang Silu and censor-in-chief Deng Jingshan were made deputies; vice minister of revenue Li Yi was made campaign marshal; censor Song Ruosi, drafting attendant Jia Zhi, and right bureau director Wei Shaoyou were made administrators; and attendant Liu Zhi was made staff planner.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Silu, Minister of War, and Deng Jingshan, chief censor, became his deputies; Li Yi, vice minister of revenue, was made campaign marshal; Song Ruosi, Jia Zhi, and Wei Shaoyou served as administrators; and Liu Zhi, imperial attendant, was made staff planner.

sentences.zh: 琯分三軍趨京師：楊希文將南軍，自宜壽入；

translations.literal: Guan divided three armies to advance on the capital: Yang Xiwen commanded the southern army, entering from Yishou;
translations.idiomatic: Guan divided his force into three columns marching on the capital: Yang Xiwen led the southern army in from Yishou;

sentences.zh: 劉悊將中軍，自武功入；

translations.literal: Liu Ti commanded the central army, entering from Wugong;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ti led the central army in from Wugong;

sentences.zh: 李光進將北軍，自奉天入。

translations.literal: Li Guangjin commanded the northern army, entering from Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangjin led the northern army in from Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 琯身中軍先鋒。

translations.literal: Guan himself was vanguard of the central army.
translations.idiomatic: Guan himself rode at the head of the central column.

sentences.zh: 十月庚子，次便橋。

translations.literal: On the gengzi day of the tenth month he halted at Bian Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day of the tenth month he encamped at Bian Bridge.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，中軍、北軍遇賊陳濤斜，戰不利。

translations.literal: On xinchou the central and northern armies met the rebels at Chen-Tao Slope; the battle went badly.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the central and northern columns met the rebels at Chen-Tao Slope and were beaten.

sentences.zh: 琯欲持重有所伺，中人邢延恩促戰，故敗，士死麻葦。

translations.literal: Guan wished to act with weight and wait for an opportunity; the eunuch Xing Yan'en urged battle, and therefore they were defeated; soldiers died thick as hemp and reeds.
translations.idiomatic: Guan had wanted to move cautiously and watch for an opening, but the eunuch Xing Yan'en pressed for battle, and the defeat left the dead piled like hemp stalks in a field.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，率南軍復戰，遂大敗，希文、悊皆降賊。

translations.literal: On guimao he led the southern army to fight again and suffered a great defeat; Xiwen and Ti both surrendered to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later he led the southern army into battle again and was routed; Xiwen and Ti both went over to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 初，琯用春秋時戰法，以車二千乘繚營，騎步夾之。

translations.literal: At the outset Guan employed Spring and Autumn period battle methods, with two thousand chariots encircling the camp and cavalry and infantry flanking them.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset Guan had deployed Spring and Autumn–style tactics: two thousand war chariots ringed the camp with cavalry and infantry on either flank.

sentences.zh: 既戰，賊乘風噪，牛悉髀栗，賊投芻而火之，人畜焚燒，殺卒四萬，血丹野，殘眾才數千，不能軍。

translations.literal: Once battle was joined, the rebels rode the wind with clamor; the oxen all trembled in the hindquarters; the rebels threw fodder and set it afire; men and beasts were burned; forty thousand soldiers were killed; blood reddened the wilds; the remnant force was only several thousand and could not form an army.
translations.idiomatic: When battle was joined the rebels raised a wind of noise; the oxen shook in terror; the rebels threw fodder and torched it; men and beasts burned; forty thousand soldiers died and the plain ran red; only a few thousand survivors remained, unable to regroup as an army.

sentences.zh: 琯還走行在，見帝，肉袒請罪，帝宥之，使裒夷散，復圖進取。

translations.literal: Guan fled back to the imperial camp, saw the emperor, bared his torso to beg punishment; the emperor pardoned him, had him gather and bury the scattered dead, and again plan an advance.
translations.idiomatic: Guan fled back to the imperial camp, bared his torso to beg forgiveness, and was pardoned; the emperor had him gather and bury the dead and plan another advance.

sentences.zh: 琯雅自負，以天下為己任，然用兵本非所長。

translations.literal: Guan was by nature self-confident and took the realm as his own charge, yet employing troops was fundamentally not his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Guan was naturally self-assured and took the fate of the realm as his personal charge, but command of armies was never his gift.

sentences.zh: 其佐李揖、劉秩等皆儒生，未嘗更軍旅，琯每詫曰：「彼曳落河雖多，能當我劉秩乎？」

translations.literal: His aides Li Yi, Liu Zhi, and the rest were all Confucian scholars who had never experienced military service; Guan would often boast, saying: "Though those Tiele tribesmen are many, can they match my Liu Zhi?
translations.idiomatic: His aides Li Yi, Liu Zhi, and the rest were scholars who had never seen war; Guan would boast, "However many Tiele warriors they field, can they stand against my Liu Zhi?

sentences.zh: 帝雖恨琯喪師，而眷任未衰。

translations.literal: Though the emperor resented Guan's loss of the army, his favor and trust did not wane.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor resented the loss of the army, his regard for Guan did not yet fade.

sentences.zh: 崔圓自蜀來，最後見帝，琯謂帝不見省，易之。

translations.literal: Cui Yuan came from Shu and was the last to see the emperor; Guan said the emperor had not received him and replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuan came up from Shu and was the last of the ministers to be received by the emperor; Guan said the emperor had overlooked him and had him replaced.

sentences.zh: 圓以金畀李輔國，不淹日被寵，遂怨琯。

translations.literal: Yuan gave gold to Li Fuguo; within a short time he won favor and thereupon bore resentment toward Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan paid Li Fuguo a bribe and within days won the emperor's favor, then turned against Guan.

sentences.zh: 琯數稱疾不入。

translations.literal: Guan repeatedly claimed illness and did not enter court.
translations.idiomatic: Guan repeatedly pleaded illness and stayed away from court.

sentences.zh: 會御史大夫顏真卿劾奏諫議大夫李何忌不孝，琯素善何忌，不欲以惡名錮之，托被酒入朝，貶西平郡司馬。

translations.literal: When censor-in-chief Yan Zhenqing impeached remonstrating grand master Li Heji for unfilial conduct, Guan had long been on good terms with Heji and did not wish to imprison him under an evil name; he pretended to be drunk entering court and was demoted to military adjutant of Xiping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Zhenqing, censor-in-chief, impeached remonstrating grand master Li Heji for unfilial conduct, Guan, who had long favored Heji and did not want him ruined by the charge, entered court pretending to be drunk and was demoted to military adjutant of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 琴工董廷蘭出入琯所，琯昵之。

translations.literal: The lute artisan Dong Yanlan came and went at Guan's residence; Guan was intimate with him.
translations.idiomatic: The lutenist Dong Yanlan frequented Guan's house, and Guan favored him.

sentences.zh: 廷蘭藉琯勢，數招賕謝，為有司劾治，琯訴於帝，帝因震怒，叱遣之，琯惶恐就第。

translations.literal: Yanlan relied on Guan's power and repeatedly solicited bribes and gifts; he was impeached by the authorities; Guan appealed to the emperor; the emperor thereupon was shaken to anger, shouted and dismissed him; Guan in fear withdrew to his mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Yanlan used Guan's influence to solicit bribes repeatedly until the authorities impeached him; Guan appealed to the emperor, who flew into a rage, shouted him down, and sent him away; Guan withdrew to his mansion in fear.

sentences.zh: 罷為太子少師。

translations.literal: He was removed and made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed to the post of Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 從帝還都，封清河郡公。

translations.literal: Following the emperor's return to the capital, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 琯之廢，朝臣多言琯謀包文武，可復用，雖琯亦自謂當柄任，為天子立功。

translations.literal: After Guan's dismissal, many court officials said Guan's plans embraced both civil and military affairs and he could be employed again; even Guan himself said he ought to hold the helm and render achievement for the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: After Guan's fall many officials said his plans combined civil and military talent and that he could serve again; Guan himself believed he should hold power once more and win merit for the throne.

sentences.zh: 善琯者暴其言於朝。

translations.literal: Those who favored Guan spread his words at court.
translations.idiomatic: His supporters repeated these boasts at court.

sentences.zh: 琯方日引劉秩、嚴武與宴語，移病自如。

translations.literal: Guan was then daily inviting Liu Zhi and Yan Wu to feast and converse, pleading illness as before.
translations.idiomatic: Guan spent his days feasting and talking with Liu Zhi and Yan Wu while continuing to plead illness as an excuse.

sentences.zh: 帝以琯虛言浮誕，內鞅鞅，挾黨背公，非大臣體。

translations.literal: The emperor considered Guan's words empty and frivolous, inwardly discontent, clinging to factions against the public good—not the bearing of a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged Guan's talk empty and reckless, resented his inner discontent, and saw faction-mongering against the public good—conduct unworthy of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年，出琯為邠州刺史，逐秩、武等，因下詔陳其比周狀，喻敕中外。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianyuan Guan was sent out as prefect of Binzhou; Liu Zhi, Yan Wu, and the rest were expelled; an edict was thereupon issued stating his factional conduct, instructing court and realm.
translations.idiomatic: In 758 Guan was sent out as prefect of Bin; Liu Zhi, Yan Wu, and the rest were driven off, and an edict detailed his cliquish conduct for the whole court and empire.

sentences.zh: 始，邠以武將領刺史，故綱目廢弛，即治府為營，吏攘民居相淆歡。

translations.literal: At the outset Bin was led by a military general as prefect, and therefore regulations were lax; the prefectural offices were turned into barracks; clerks seized civilian dwellings in confused mingling.
translations.idiomatic: Bin had long been run by generals serving as prefect, so government had collapsed: the prefectural compound was a barracks, and officials had seized civilian homes at will.

sentences.zh: 琯至，一切革之，人以便安，政聲流聞。

translations.literal: When Guan arrived he reformed everything; the people found convenience and peace; his governmental reputation spread.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan arrived he reformed everything; the people found life easier, and word of his good government spread.

sentences.zh: 召拜太子賓客，遷禮部尚書，為晉、漢二州刺史。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Guest of the Heir Apparent, promoted to Minister of Rites, and served as prefect of the two prefectures Jin and Han.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Guest of the Heir Apparent, promoted to Minister of Rites, and later served as prefect of Jin and Han.

sentences.zh: 寶應二年，召拜刑部尚書，道病卒，贈太尉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoying he was summoned and appointed Minister of Justice; on the road he fell ill and died; posthumously he was made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In 763 he was recalled as Minister of Justice but fell ill on the journey and died; he was posthumously made Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 琯有遠器，好談老子、浮屠法，喜賓客，高談有餘，而不切事。

translations.literal: Guan had far-reaching capacity, loved to discuss Laozi and Buddhist law, delighted in guests, had lofty talk in abundance, yet was not practical in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Guan had breadth of vision, loved discourse on Laozi and Buddhism, delighted in entertaining guests, and talked brilliantly—but without practical grip on affairs.

sentences.zh: 時天下多故，急於謀略攻取，帝以吏事繩下，而琯為相，遽欲從容鎮靜以輔治之，又知人不明，以取敗撓，故功名隳損云。

translations.literal: At the time the realm had many troubles and urgency lay in strategy and conquest; the emperor bound subordinates with administrative affairs, yet Guan as chancellor abruptly wished to assist governance through leisurely calm and composure; moreover he did not discern men clearly and thereby brought defeat and obstruction—therefore his fame and achievement were ruined, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was in turmoil and demanded strategy and conquest; the emperor ruled through strict administration, yet Guan as chancellor wanted at once to steady the state through unhurried calm. He also misjudged men and brought defeat on himself—so his fame and achievement collapsed.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：唐名儒多言琯德器，有王佐材，而史載行事，亦少貶矣。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Tang's famous Confucians often spoke of Guan's virtue and capacity, that he had material to assist a king, yet the history records his conduct and also offers some disparagement.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Tang's leading scholars often praised Guan's character and talent and called him fit to assist a king, yet the historical record of his deeds offers its own reproach.

sentences.zh: 一舉喪師，訖不復振。

translations.literal: One campaign lost the army, and to the end he did not revive.
translations.idiomatic: One defeat cost him the army, and he never recovered.

sentences.zh: 原琯以忠誼自奮，片言悟主而取宰相，必有以過人者，用違所長，遂無成功。

translations.literal: Tracing Guan: he roused himself through loyalty and righteousness; a few words moved his lord and won the chancellery—he must have had something surpassing others; employed contrary to his strengths, he therefore had no success.
translations.idiomatic: Consider Guan: he drove himself by loyalty and duty, won the chancellery with a few words that moved his sovereign, and plainly had gifts above the common run—yet he was used against his strengths and achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 然盛名之下，為難居矣。

translations.literal: Yet beneath a great name, it is hard to dwell.
translations.idiomatic: Yet it is hard to live up to a great name.

sentences.zh: 夫名盛則責望備，實不副則訾咎深。

translations.literal: When fame is great, expectations are complete; when reality does not match, blame runs deep.
translations.idiomatic: Great fame raises complete expectations; when reality falls short, blame runs deep.

sentences.zh: 使琯遭時承平，從容帷幄，不失為名宰。

translations.literal: Had Guan encountered a time of peace and stability, conducting affairs at leisure within the tent, he would not have failed to be a renowned minister.
translations.idiomatic: Had Guan lived in a peaceful age and steered policy calmly from the council chamber, he might still have been remembered as a fine minister.

sentences.zh: 而倉卒濟難，事敗隙生，陷於浮虛比周之罪，名之為累也，戒哉！

translations.literal: Yet in haste to rescue difficulty, affairs failed and rifts arose; he fell into the crimes of emptiness and faction—fame becomes a burden; take warning!
translations.idiomatic: But pressed to save the dynasty in crisis, he failed, cracks opened, and he fell under charges of empty talk and cliquishness—reputation became his burden. Let that be a warning!

sentences.zh: 子 孺復子孺復，幼頗能屬文，然狂縱不法。

translations.literal: Son: Ru Fu. Ru Fu in his youth could compose texts rather well, yet was wild and unrestrained and lawless.
translations.idiomatic: Son: Ru Fu. Ru Fu could write passably well from youth, but was wild, unrestrained, and lawless.

sentences.zh: 淮南節度使陳少游奏置幕府。

translations.literal: Huainan military commissioner Chen Shaoyou memorialized to place him in the staff bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan military commissioner Chen Shaoyou had him appointed to his staff.

sentences.zh: 多招術家言己三十當得宰相，以熏權近，希進取。

translations.literal: He recruited many occult specialists who said that at thirty he would obtain the chancellery, thereby influencing those near power and hoping for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered diviners who told him he would reach the chancellery at thirty, curried favor with those near power, and schemed for promotion.

sentences.zh: 後辟浙西韓滉府。

translations.literal: Later he was recruited into Zhexi Han Huang's staff.
translations.idiomatic: Later he entered the staff of Han Huang in Zhexi.

sentences.zh: 兄宗偃喪自嶺外還，孺復不出臨吊。

translations.literal: When his elder brother Zongyan's coffin returned from beyond the ranges, Ru Fu did not come out to attend the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When his elder brother Zongyan's coffin returned from the south, Ru Fu did not come out to mourn.

sentences.zh: 與妻鄭不相中，慈姆為言，乃具棺召家人生斂之；

translations.literal: He and his wife Zheng did not get along; the kindly nurse spoke for her, and he thereupon prepared a coffin and summoned the household to perform the encoffining while she still lived;
translations.idiomatic: He and his wife Zheng were at odds; when the nurse pleaded for her, he had a coffin prepared and called the household to perform the encoffining rite while she was still alive;

sentences.zh: 鄭方乳，促上道，鄭死於行。

translations.literal: Zheng was still nursing; he urged her onto the road; Zheng died on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was still nursing an infant; he hurried her onto the road, and she died on the way.

sentences.zh: 又娶崔昭女，崔悍媢，殺二侍兒，私瘞之。

translations.literal: He again married a daughter of Cui Zhao; Cui was fierce and jealous, killed two maidservants, and secretly buried them.
translations.idiomatic: He then married a daughter of Cui Zhao; she was fierce and jealous, killed two maidservants, and buried them in secret.

sentences.zh: 觀察使以聞，貶連州司馬，聽崔去。

translations.literal: The observation commissioner reported it; he was demoted to military adjutant of Lianzhou; Cui was allowed to leave.
translations.idiomatic: The observation commissioner reported the matter; Ru Fu was demoted to military adjutant of Lianzhou and Cui was permitted to leave him.

sentences.zh: 既又與崔通，請復合，詔許。

translations.literal: Afterward he again had relations with Cui and requested reunion; an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: He later resumed relations with Cui and asked to take her back; the court allowed it.

sentences.zh: 未幾復離。

translations.literal: Before long they separated again.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they parted again.

sentences.zh: 終容州刺史。

translations.literal: He ended as prefect of Rongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as prefect of Rongzhou.

sentences.zh: 孫 啟琯孫啟，以廕補鳳翔參軍事，累調萬年令，素贅附王叔文。

translations.literal: Grandson: Qi. Guan's grandson Qi, through yin privilege was made staff officer at Fengxiang, was repeatedly transferred to magistrate of Wannian, and had long attached himself to Wang Shuwen.
translations.idiomatic: Grandson: Qi. Guan's grandson Qi entered service at Fengxiang by hereditary privilege, rose to magistrate of Wannian, and had long clung to Wang Shuwen's faction.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，叔文用事，除容管經略使，陰許以荊南帥節。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenyuan Shuwen held power; Qi was appointed Rongguan frontier commissioner, with a secret promise of the Jingnan commander's seal.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhenyuan era, when Shuwen held power, Qi was made frontier commissioner of Rongguan with a secret promise of the Jingnan command.

sentences.zh: 啟至荊湖，宿留不肯進，會叔文與韋執誼內忿爭，不果拜。

translations.literal: Qi reached Jing-Hu, lingered and would not advance; when Shuwen and Wei Zhiyi quarreled inwardly, the appointment did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: Qi reached the Jing-Hu region and lingered without advancing; when Shuwen and Wei Zhiyi fell out among themselves, the promised appointment never materialized.

sentences.zh: 俄而皇太子監國，啟惶駭就鎮。

translations.literal: Soon the crown prince became regent of the realm; Qi in fear and alarm took up his post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the crown prince assumed regency; Qi, terrified, hurried to his post.

sentences.zh: 凡九年，改桂管觀察使。

translations.literal: In all nine years he was changed to Guiguan observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After nine years he was transferred to observation commissioner of Guiguan.

sentences.zh: 州邸以賂請有司飛驛送詔，既而憲宗自遣宦人持詔賜啟，啟畏使者邀重餉，即曰：「先五日已得詔。」

translations.literal: The prefectural residence used bribes to ask the authorities to dispatch the edict by urgent relay; afterward Emperor Xianzong himself sent a eunuch bearing the edict to bestow on Qi; Qi feared the envoy would demand heavy gifts and immediately said: "Five days ago I already received the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural residence bribed officials to have the edict sent by urgent relay; then Xianzong himself sent a eunuch with the appointment. Qi, fearing the envoy would demand a heavy gift, said at once, "I received the edict five days ago.

sentences.zh: 使者紿請視，因馳歸以聞，貶太僕少卿。

translations.literal: The envoy deceived him into asking to see it and thereupon galloped back to report; Qi was demoted to vice minister of the stud.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy tricked him into asking to see it, then galloped back to report the lie; Qi was demoted to vice minister of the stud.

sentences.zh: 啟自陳獻使者南口十五，帝怒，殺宦人，貶啟虔州長史，死。

translations.literal: Qi himself stated that he had given the envoy fifteen [units] from Nankou; the emperor was angry, executed the eunuch, and demoted Qi to chief administrator of Ganzhou; he died.
translations.idiomatic: Qi admitted he had given the envoy fifteen [units] from Nankou; the emperor was furious, executed the eunuch, demoted Qi to chief administrator of Ganzhou, and Qi died.

sentences.zh: 始詔五管、福建、黔中道不得以口饋遺、博易，罷臘口等使。

translations.literal: At the outset an edict forbade the Five Circuits, Fujian, and Qianzhong circuit from using human tribute for gifts and trade, and abolished the Lakou and similar commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon an edict forbade the Five Circuits, Fujian, and Qianzhong from trading in human tribute and abolished the Lakou commissioners and the like.

sentences.zh: 族孫 式琯族孫式，擢進士第，累遷忠州刺史。

translations.literal: Descendant of the clan: Shi. Guan's clansman descendant Shi passed the jinshi examination, was repeatedly promoted to prefect of Zhongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Clansman descendant: Shi. Guan's kinsman Shi passed the jinshi examination and rose to prefect of Zhong.

sentences.zh: 韋皋表為雲南安撫副使、蜀州刺史。

translations.literal: Wei Gao memorialized him as vice commissioner for Yunnan pacification and prefect of Shuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao recommended him as vice commissioner for Yunnan pacification and prefect of Shu.

sentences.zh: 皋卒，劉辟反，式留不得行。

translations.literal: When Gao died, Liu Pi rebelled; Shi was detained and could not leave.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao died, Liu Pi rebelled, and Shi was trapped and unable to leave.

sentences.zh: 賊平，高崇文保貸之，言諸朝，除吏部郎中。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, Gao Chongwen guaranteed and vouched for him, spoke of him at court, and he was appointed director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed, Gao Chongwen stood surety for him and spoke on his behalf at court; he was appointed director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時河朔諸將劉濟、張茂昭等更相劾奏，帝欲和之，拜式給事中，使河北，還奏如旨。

translations.literal: At the time the Hebei generals Liu Ji, Zhang Maozhao, and others impeached one another in turn; the emperor wished to reconcile them, appointed Shi as imperial attendant, sent him to Hebei, and on his return he memorialized as the emperor wished.
translations.idiomatic: The Hebei generals Liu Ji, Zhang Maozhao, and others were impeaching one another; the emperor wanted reconciliation, made Shi imperial attendant, sent him to Hebei, and his report on return matched the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 遷陝虢觀察使，改河南尹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to observation commissioner of Shan-Guo and changed to Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was made observation commissioner of Shan-Guo, then Intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 會討王承宗鎮州，索餉車四千乘，民不能具。

translations.literal: When the campaign against Wang Chengzong at Zhenzhou was underway, four thousand supply carts were demanded; the people could not furnish them.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Wang Chengzong at Zhenzhou, the court demanded four thousand supply carts, which the people could not provide.

sentences.zh: 式建言：「歲凶人勞，不任調發。」

translations.literal: Shi memorialized, saying: "The year is harsh and the people weary; they cannot bear requisition and dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Shi memorialized: "The harvest has failed and the people are exhausted; they cannot bear another levy.

sentences.zh: 又御史元稹亦言：「賊未禽，而河南民先困。」

translations.literal: Censor Yuan Zhen also said: "The rebels are not yet captured, yet the people of Henan are already distressed."
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yuan Zhen also said, "The rebels are not yet taken, yet the people of Henan are already in distress."

sentences.zh: 詔可，都鄙安之。

translations.literal: An edict approved it; capital and countryside were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved the relief, and the capital and countryside were reassured.

sentences.zh: 改宣歙觀察使。

translations.literal: He was changed to observation commissioner of Xuan-She.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to observation commissioner of Xuan-She.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈左散騎常侍，諡曰傾。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Left Regular Attendant; his posthumous name was Qing.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Left Regular Attendant with the posthumous name Qing.

sentences.zh: 吏部郎中韋乾度曰：「始式刺蜀州，劉辟構難，即謂辟曰：『向夢公為上相，儀衛甚盛，幸無相忘。』

translations.literal: Director in the Ministry of Personnel Wei Qiandu said: "When Shi first governed Shuzhou, Liu Pi raised trouble; he immediately told Pi: 'I lately dreamed that you became chief minister with very grand guards and retinue—may you not forget me.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Qiandu, director in the Ministry of Personnel, said: "When Shi first governed Shu, Liu Pi rebelled; Shi at once told Pi, 'I dreamed you became chief minister with a grand guard of honor—do not forget me when you rise.

sentences.zh: 辟喜，以為祥。

translations.literal: Pi was pleased and took it as an auspicious omen.
translations.idiomatic: Pi was delighted and took it as a good omen.

sentences.zh: 後辟發兵署牒，首曰辟，副曰式，參謀曰符載。

translations.literal: Later when Pi raised troops and issued orders, the first name was Pi, the second Shi, and staff planner Fu Zai.
translations.idiomatic: When Pi later mobilized troops, his orders listed Pi first, Shi second, and Fu Zai as staff planner.

sentences.zh: 大節已虧，不宜得諡。」

translations.literal: His great integrity was already impaired; he ought not receive a posthumous name.'
translations.idiomatic: His great integrity was already compromised; he should not receive a posthumous name.'

sentences.zh: 博士李虞仲曰：「始辟反，為其用者皆救死其頸，可盡被惡名乎？

translations.literal: Erudite Li Yuzhong said: "When Pi first rebelled, those employed by him all strove to save their necks—can they all bear evil names?
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Li Yuzhong said, "When Pi first rebelled, everyone in his service scrambled to save his own neck—must they all bear a villain's name?

sentences.zh: 如式，不能去，又不能死，可謂求生害仁者也。

translations.literal: As for Shi, he could not leave, yet could not die—one may say he harmed benevolence to preserve life.
translations.idiomatic: As for Shi, he could neither leave nor die—he harmed benevolence to save his own life.

sentences.zh: 辟走西山，召所疑畏者盡殺之，式在其間，會救得免。

translations.literal: Pi fled to Western Mountain, summoned those he suspected and feared and killed them all; Shi was among them but by chance was rescued and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Pi fled to Western Mountain and summoned those he feared to kill them all; Shi was among them but was rescued in time.

sentences.zh: 而曰大節已虧，近於溢言。」

translations.literal: Yet to say his great integrity was impaired comes close to excessive words."
translations.idiomatic: Yet to say his great integrity was lost comes close to exaggeration."

sentences.zh: 諡乃定。

translations.literal: The posthumous name was thereupon fixed.
translations.idiomatic: The posthumous name was then confirmed.

sentences.zh: 張鎬，字從周，博州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Gao, styled Congzhou, was a native of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gao, whose courtesy name was Congzhou, came from Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 儀狀瑰偉，有大志，視經史猶漁獵，然好王霸大略。

translations.literal: His bearing was magnificent and grand; he had great ambition; he treated the classics and histories like fishing and hunting, yet loved kingly and hegemonic grand strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He was imposing in bearing and ambitious; he treated the classics like sport, yet loved grand strategy fit for emperors and hegemons.

sentences.zh: 少事吳兢，兢器之。

translations.literal: In youth he served Wu Jing; Jing valued his talent.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he served Wu Jing, who prized his ability.

sentences.zh: 游京師，未知名，率嗜酒鼓琴自娛。

translations.literal: Traveling in the capital, still unknown, he generally loved wine and strumming the zither for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital, still unknown, he mostly amused himself with wine and the zither.

sentences.zh: 人或邀之，杖策往，醉即返，不及世務。

translations.literal: When someone invited him, he went leaning on his staff; when drunk he returned, not reaching to worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When invited he would go leaning on his staff, return when drunk, and pay no heed to worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，楊國忠執政，求天下士為己重，聞鎬才，薦之。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao Yang Guozhong held power, sought men of talent throughout the realm to add to his weight, heard of Gao's ability, and recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianbao era Yang Guozhong held power and sought talented men to bolster his faction; hearing of Gao's ability, he recommended him.

sentences.zh: 釋褐衣，拜左拾遺，歷侍御史。

translations.literal: He doffed commoner's dress, was appointed Left Remonstrator, and passed through attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: He left commoner's dress behind, was appointed Left Remonstrator, and later served as attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 玄宗西狩，鎬徒步扈從。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong hunted westward, Gao followed on foot in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong fled west, Gao followed on foot in attendance.

sentences.zh: 俄遣詣肅宗所。

translations.literal: Soon he was dispatched to Suzong's location.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent to Suzong's camp.

sentences.zh: 數論事，擢諫議大夫，尋拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He repeatedly discussed affairs; was promoted to remonstrating grand master; soon was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and co-chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke repeatedly on policy, was promoted to remonstrating grand master, and soon made Vice Director of the Secretariat and co-chancellor.

sentences.zh: 時引內浮屠數百居禁中，號「內道場」，諷唄外聞，鎬諫曰：「天子之福，要在養人，以一函宇，美風化，未聞區區佛法而致太平。

translations.literal: At the time several hundred Buddhist monks were brought within the palace, called the 'Inner Way-place'; chanting was heard outside; Gao remonstrated, saying: "The Son of Heaven's blessing lies in nourishing the people, in one realm under heaven beautifying customs and transformation—one has not heard that petty Buddhist law brings great peace.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of Buddhist monks had been brought into the palace in what was called the Inner Way-place, and their chanting could be heard outside. Gao remonstrated: "A Son of Heaven's blessing lies in nourishing his people and civilizing the realm—not in petty Buddhist rites bringing peace.

sentences.zh: 願陛下以無為為心，不以小乘撓聖慮。」

translations.literal: May Your Majesty take non-action as heart, and not let the lesser vehicle disturb the sage's deliberations."
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty keep non-action at heart and not let lesser Buddhist teaching disturb your sacred deliberations."

sentences.zh: 帝然之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 尋詔兼河南節度使，都統淮南諸軍事。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered additionally as Henan military commissioner and overall commander of Huainan military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to serve additionally as military commissioner of Henan and overall commander of Huainan forces.

sentences.zh: 賊圍宋州，張巡告急，鎬倍道進，檄濠州刺史閭丘曉趣救。

translations.literal: Rebels besieged Songzhou; Zhang Xun reported urgency; Gao advanced by double marches and issued an order to Hao prefect Lüqiu Xiao to hurry to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels besieged Songzhou; Zhang Xun sent urgent appeals; Gao marched at forced pace and ordered Hao prefect Lüqiu Xiao to hurry to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 曉愎撓，逗留不肯進，比鎬至淮口，而巡已陷。

translations.literal: Xiao was obstinate and hesitant, lingered and would not advance; by the time Gao reached the Huai mouth, Xun had already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao was obstinate, lingered, and refused to advance; by the time Gao reached the Huai mouth, Xun had already fallen.

sentences.zh: 鎬怒，杖殺曉。

translations.literal: Gao in anger had Xiao beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Gao in fury had Xiao beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 帝還京師，封南陽郡公，詔以本軍鎮汴州，捕平殘寇。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to the capital, Gao was enfeoffed Duke of Nanyang commandery; he was ordered to station his army at Bianzhou and capture and pacify remnant bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital, Gao was enfeoffed Duke of Nanyang and ordered to station his army at Bianzhou to hunt down remnant rebels.

sentences.zh: 史思明提范陽獻順款，鎬揣其偽，密奏曰：「思明勢窮而服，包藏不測，可以計取，難以義招，不宜以威權假之。」

translations.literal: Shi Siming from Fanyang offered submission; Gao judged it false and secretly memorialized, saying: "Siming submits because his power is exhausted; he harbors the unforeseeable; he may be taken by stratagem, hard to win by righteousness—authority and power should not be lent him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming from Fanyang offered submission; Gao judged it deceitful and secretly memorialized: "Siming submits only because he is cornered; he harbors unknown designs; he can be taken by stratagem, not won by righteousness—do not lend him authority.

sentences.zh: 又言：「滑州防禦使許叔冀狡獪，臨難必變，宜追還宿衛。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Huazhou defense commissioner Xu Shuji is crafty; facing crisis he will surely change—he should be recalled to palace guard duty."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Huazhou defense commissioner Xu Shuji is crafty and will turn in a crisis—recall him to palace guard duty."

sentences.zh: 書入不省。

translations.literal: The memorial entered but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was ignored.

sentences.zh: 時宦官絡繹出鎬境，未嘗降情結納。

translations.literal: At the time eunuchs continuously passed through Gao's territory; he had never lowered himself to win them over.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs constantly passed through his territory, yet he never stooped to court them.

sentences.zh: 自范陽、滑州使還者，皆盛言思明、叔冀忠，而毀鎬無經略才。

translations.literal: Envoys returning from Fanyang and Huazhou all lavishly praised Siming and Shuji as loyal while denigrating Gao as lacking strategic talent.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys returning from Fanyang and Huazhou all praised Siming and Shuji as loyal while denigrating Gao as lacking strategic talent.

sentences.zh: 帝以鎬不切事機，遂罷宰相，授荊州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: The emperor considered Gao not attuned to the moment's needs and thereupon dismissed him from the chancellery, appointing him chief administrator of Jingzhou metropolitan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged Gao out of touch with the moment, dismissed him from the chancellery, and made him chief administrator of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 思明、叔冀後果叛，如鎬言。

translations.literal: Siming and Shuji afterward did rebel, as Gao had said.
translations.idiomatic: Siming and Shuji later rebelled, just as Gao had predicted.

sentences.zh: 召拜太子賓客、左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Guest of the Heir Apparent and Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Guest of the Heir Apparent and Left Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 坐市嗣岐王珍第，貶辰州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: For trafficking in the Heir Apparent of Prince of Qi Zhen's mansion, he was demoted to revenue registrar of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For trafficking in property from Prince of Qi's heir Zhen's mansion, he was demoted to revenue registrar of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 代宗初，起為撫州刺史，遷洪州觀察使，更封平原郡公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daizong's reign he was raised as prefect of Fuzhou, transferred to observation commissioner of Hongzhou, and re-enfeoffed Duke of Pingyuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Daizong's reign he was restored as prefect of Fu, then made observation commissioner of Hong, and re-enfeoffed Duke of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 袁晁寇東境，江介震騷，鎬遣兵屯上饒，斬首二千級。

translations.literal: Yuan Chao raided the eastern border; the river region was shaken; Gao dispatched troops stationed at Shangrao and beheaded two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Chao raided the eastern border and shook the Yangzi region; Gao sent troops to Shangrao and took two thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 又襲舒城賊楊昭，梟之。

translations.literal: He also attacked the Shucheng bandit Yang Zhao and displayed his head.
translations.idiomatic: He also attacked the Shucheng bandit Yang Zhao and displayed his head.

sentences.zh: 沉千載者，新安大豪，連結椎剽，州縣不能禽，鎬遣別將盡殄其眾。

translations.literal: Shen Qianzai was a great magnate of Xin'an who linked up with robbers; prefectures and counties could not capture him; Gao sent a deputy general who exterminated his entire band.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Qianzai, a great magnate of Xin'an, had linked up with bandits whom the local authorities could not capture; Gao sent a deputy who exterminated his entire band.

sentences.zh: 改江南西道觀察使，卒。

translations.literal: He was changed to observation commissioner of Jiangnan West Circuit and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was made observation commissioner of Jiangnan West Circuit and died in office.

sentences.zh: 鎬起布衣，二期至宰相。

translations.literal: Gao rose from commoner's dress; in two periods he reached the chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Gao rose from commoner's dress to the chancellery in two years.

sentences.zh: 居身廉，不殖貲產。

translations.literal: In conduct he was incorrupt; he did not amass property.
translations.idiomatic: He lived incorruptibly and amassed no wealth.

sentences.zh: 善待士，性簡重，論議有體。

translations.literal: He treated scholars well; his nature was simple and weighty; his discourse had form.
translations.idiomatic: He treated scholars generously, was reserved by nature, and spoke with proper form.

sentences.zh: 在位雖淺，而天下之人推為舊德云。

translations.literal: Though his tenure was brief, people throughout the realm acclaimed him as an elder of virtue, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Though his tenure was brief, people throughout the realm hailed him as an elder statesman of virtue.

sentences.zh: 李泌，字長源，魏八柱國弼六世孫，徙居京兆。

translations.literal: Li Bi, styled Changyuan, was sixth-generation descendant of Wei Eight Pillars Bi, and migrated to reside in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bi, whose courtesy name was Changyuan, was a sixth-generation descendant of the Wei pillar Bi and had moved his family to Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 七歲知為文。

translations.literal: At seven he knew how to compose texts.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he could already write.

sentences.zh: 玄宗開元十六年，悉召能言佛、道、孔子者，相答難禁中。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Kaiyuan of Emperor Xuanzong, all who could speak on Buddhism, the Way, and Confucius were summoned to debate one another within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In 728 Xuanzong summoned everyone who could discourse on Buddhism, the Way, and Confucius to debate one another in the palace.

sentences.zh: 有員俶者，九歲升坐，詞辯注射，坐人皆屈。

translations.literal: There was Yuan Chu, nine years old, who ascended the seat; his words and debate poured forth; all seated were overcome.
translations.idiomatic: A boy named Yuan Chu, nine years old, took the seat and argued with such force that everyone present was defeated.

sentences.zh: 帝異之，曰：「半千孫，固當然。」

translations.literal: The emperor marveled at him and said: "A grandson of Banqian—naturally it should be so.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marveled and said, "A grandson of Banqian—of course he would be so.

sentences.zh: 因問：「童子豈有類若者？」

translations.literal: He thereupon asked: "Are there boys like him?"
translations.idiomatic: He then asked, "Are there other boys like him?"

sentences.zh: 俶跪奏：「臣舅子李泌。」

translations.literal: Chu knelt and memorialized: "My mother's nephew Li Bi."
translations.idiomatic: Chu knelt and said, "My cousin Li Bi."

sentences.zh: 帝即馳召之。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately sent a fast summons.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once sent for him.

sentences.zh: 泌既至，帝方與燕國公張說觀弈，因使說試其能。

translations.literal: When Bi arrived, the emperor was just watching a game of go with Duke of Yan Zhang Yue and therefore had Yue test his ability.
translations.idiomatic: When Bi arrived, the emperor was watching a game of go with Zhang Yue, Duke of Yan, and had Yue test the boy's ability.

sentences.zh: 說請賦「方圓動靜」，泌逡巡曰：「願聞其略。」

translations.literal: Yue asked him to compose on 'square, round, movement, stillness'; Bi hesitated and said: "I wish to hear the outline."
translations.idiomatic: Yue asked him to compose on square, round, movement, and stillness; Bi hesitated and said, "Please tell me the theme in brief."

sentences.zh: 說因曰：「方若棋局，圓若棋子，動若棋生，靜若棋死。」

translations.literal: Yue thereupon said: "Square like the go board, round like the go stones, movement like go coming alive, stillness like go dying."
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "Square like the board, round like the stones, movement like stones coming alive, stillness like stones dying."

sentences.zh: 泌即答曰：「方若行義，圓若用智，動若騁材，靜若得意。」

translations.literal: Bi immediately replied: "Square like practicing righteousness, round like employing wisdom, movement like displaying talent, stillness like attaining satisfaction."
translations.idiomatic: Bi answered at once, "Square like practicing righteousness, round like employing wisdom, movement like displaying talent, stillness like resting in satisfaction."

sentences.zh: 說因賀帝得奇童。

translations.literal: Yue thereupon congratulated the emperor on obtaining a wondrous child.
translations.idiomatic: Yue congratulated the emperor on gaining a prodigy.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅曰：「是子精神，要大於身。」

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and said: "This child's spirit will be greater than his body.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and said, "This child's spirit will outgrow his body.

sentences.zh: 賜束帛，敕其家曰：「善視養之。」

translations.literal: He was granted a bundle of silk and his household was ordered: "Care for and nurture him well."
translations.idiomatic: He was given silk and his family was told, "Care for him well."

sentences.zh: 張九齡尤所獎愛，常引至臥內。

translations.literal: Zhang Jiuling especially prized and loved him, often bringing him into his sleeping quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jiuling especially favored him and often brought him into his private quarters.

sentences.zh: 九齡與嚴挺之、蕭誠善，挺之惡誠佞，勸九齡謝絕之。

translations.literal: Jiuling was on good terms with Yan Tingzhi and Xiao Cheng; Tingzhi detested Cheng's flattery and urged Jiuling to break with him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling was friendly with Yan Tingzhi and Xiao Cheng; Tingzhi detested Cheng's flattery and urged Jiuling to break with him.

sentences.zh: 九齡忽獨念曰：「嚴太苦勁，然蕭軟美可喜。」

translations.literal: Jiuling suddenly thought alone: "Yan is too harsh and rigid, yet Xiao is soft and pleasing—delightful.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling suddenly mused aloud, "Yan is too harsh, yet Xiao is soft and pleasing—quite delightful.

sentences.zh: 方命左右召蕭，泌在旁，帥爾曰：「公起布衣，以直道至宰相，而喜軟美者乎？」

translations.literal: Just as he was ordering attendants to summon Xiao, Bi was at his side and abruptly said: "You rose from commoner's dress and reached the chancellery by the straight Way—yet you delight in the soft and pleasing?"
translations.idiomatic: As he ordered attendants to summon Xiao, Bi at his side said sharply, "You rose from commoner's dress to the chancellery by the straight Way—yet you delight in the soft and pleasing?"

sentences.zh: 九齡驚，改容謝之，因呼「小友」。

translations.literal: Jiuling was startled, changed expression and apologized to him, and thereupon called him 'little friend.'
translations.idiomatic: Jiuling started, changed his manner and apologized, and called him "little friend."

sentences.zh: 及長，博學，善治《易》，常游嵩、華、終南間，慕神仙不死術。

translations.literal: When grown he was broadly learned, skilled in the Changes, often traveled among Song, Hua, and Zhongnan, and admired immortal arts of not dying.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he was broadly learned, skilled in the Book of Changes, often traveled among Mount Song, Mount Hua, and Zhongnan, and sought immortal arts.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，詣闕獻《復明堂九鼎議》，帝憶其早惠，召講《老子》，有法，得待詔翰林，仍供奉東宮，皇太子遇之厚。

translations.literal: During Tianbao he came to court and presented 'Memorial on Restoring the Bright Hall and Nine Cauldrons'; the emperor recalled his early precocity, summoned him to lecture on the Laozi—he had method—and was made Hanlin attendant, still serving the Eastern Palace; the crown prince treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianbao he came to court with a memorial on restoring the Bright Hall and Nine Cauldrons; the emperor recalled his childhood brilliance, summoned him to lecture on the Laozi with real mastery, made him Hanlin attendant, and kept him at the Eastern Palace, where the crown prince treated him generously.

sentences.zh: 嘗賦詩譏誚楊國忠、安祿山等，國忠疾之，詔斥置蘄春郡。

translations.literal: He once composed poetry mocking Yang Guozhong, An Lushan, and others; Guozhong resented him; an edict dismissed him to Qichun commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote poetry mocking Yang Guozhong, An Lushan, and others; Guozhong resented it and he was banished to Qichun.

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位靈武，物色求訪，會泌亦自至。

translations.literal: When Suzong took the throne at Lingwu, he sought and inquired after him; it happened that Bi also came of himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong took the throne at Lingwu he sought him out, and Bi arrived on his own.

sentences.zh: 已謁見，陳天下所以成敗事，帝悅，欲授以官，固辭，願以客從。

translations.literal: After he had been received in audience, he set forth the reasons for the realm's success and failure; the emperor was pleased and wished to grant him office; he firmly declined and wished to follow as a guest.
translations.idiomatic: After audience he explained why the realm had succeeded or failed; the emperor was pleased and wished to give him office, but he firmly declined and asked to follow as a private guest.

sentences.zh: 入議國事，出陪輿輦，眾指曰：「著黃者聖人，著白者山人。」

translations.literal: Entering to discuss state affairs, going out to accompany the imperial carriage, the crowd pointed and said: "The one in yellow is the sage; the one in white is the mountain man.
translations.idiomatic: He entered to discuss state affairs and went out beside the imperial carriage; people pointed and said, "The one in yellow is the sage; the one in white is the mountain man.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，因賜金紫，拜元帥廣平王行軍司馬。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and thereupon granted gold and purple; he was appointed campaign marshal to the marshal Prince of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard and granted him gold and purple robes, appointing him campaign marshal to Marshal Prince of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗曰「卿侍上皇，中為朕師，今下判廣平行軍，朕父子資卿道義」云。

translations.literal: The emperor once said: "You served the Retired Emperor, in the middle were teacher to Us, now below you judge Guangping's campaign—We father and son rely on your Way and righteousness," it is said.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once said, "You served the retired emperor, were my teacher in between, and now serve under Guangping's command—my father and I rely on your moral guidance."

sentences.zh: 始，軍中謀帥，皆屬建甯王，泌密白帝曰：「建甯王誠賢，然廣平塚嗣，有君人量，豈使為吳太伯乎？」

translations.literal: At the outset the army discussed commanders and all looked to Prince of Jianning; Bi secretly informed the emperor, saying: "Prince of Jianning is indeed worthy, yet Guangping is heir in the main line and has the measure of a ruler—how could he be made like Wu Taibo?
translations.idiomatic: At first the army favored Prince of Jianning as commander; Bi secretly told the emperor, "Jianning is worthy, but Guangping is the legitimate heir and has the measure of a ruler—would you make him another Taibo of Wu?

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「廣平為太子，何假元帥？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Guangping is crown prince—why borrow the title of marshal?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Guangping is already crown prince—why does he need the marshal's title?"

sentences.zh: 泌曰：「使元帥有功，陛下不以為儲副，得耶？

translations.literal: Bi said: "If the marshal has achievement, would Your Majesty not make him heir—can that be?
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "If the marshal wins merit, could you refuse to make him heir?

sentences.zh: 太子從曰撫軍，守曰監國，今元帥乃撫軍也。」

translations.literal: The crown prince going out is styled 'military overseer,' staying in is styled 'regent of the realm'—now the marshal is military overseer."
translations.idiomatic: A crown prince leaving court is styled 'military overseer,' staying in is 'regent of the realm'—the marshal's post is the overseer's role."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this.

sentences.zh: 初，帝在東宮，李林甫數構譖，勢危甚，及即位，怨之，欲掘塚焚骨。

translations.literal: At the outset, when the emperor was in the Eastern Palace, Li Linfu repeatedly fabricated slanders and his position was very perilous; when he took the throne he resented him and wished to dig up the grave and burn the bones.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor had been crown prince, Li Linfu had repeatedly slandered him and put him in grave danger; on taking the throne he bore a grudge and wished to dig up Linfu's grave and burn his bones.

sentences.zh: 泌以天子而念宿嫌，示天下不廣，使脅從之徒得釋言於賊。

translations.literal: Bi considered that for the Son of Heaven to brood on old grievances showed the realm was not broad, and let those coerced into following give voice to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Bi argued that for a Son of Heaven to nurse old grudges showed the realm was not magnanimous and would let those coerced into rebellion speak for the enemy.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅，曰：「往事卿忘之乎？」

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and said: "Have you forgotten the past affairs?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and said, "Have you forgotten what he did?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣念不在此。

translations.literal: He replied: "My concern is not here.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "My concern lies elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 上皇有天下五十年，一旦失意，南方氣候惡，且春秋高，聞陛下錄故怨，將內慚不懌，萬有一感疾，是陛下以天下之廣不能安親也。」

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor held the realm for fifty years; in a moment he lost his wish; the southern climate is harsh and moreover his years are advanced; hearing that Your Majesty pursues old resentments, he will inwardly feel shame and displeasure; if by any chance he is stricken ill, this is Your Majesty using the breadth of the realm yet unable to put a parent at ease."
translations.idiomatic: The retired emperor held the realm for fifty years, then lost everything; the southern climate is harsh and he is old; if he hears you pursuing old grudges he will be ashamed and distressed; should he fall ill, you would have the whole realm yet fail to comfort your own father."

sentences.zh: 帝感悟，抱泌頸以泣曰：「朕不及此。」

translations.literal: The emperor was moved to understanding, embraced Bi's neck and wept, saying: "We did not reach this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved, embraced Bi's neck, and wept, "I had not thought of that."

sentences.zh: 因從容問破賊期，對曰；

translations.literal: Thereupon at leisure he asked when the rebels would be broken; he replied:
translations.idiomatic: He then casually asked when the rebels would be defeated; Bi replied:

sentences.zh: 「賊掠金帛子女，悉送范陽，有苟得心，渠能定中國邪？

translations.literal: "The rebels plunder gold, silk, and women and children, all sending them to Fanyang; having attained a moment's satisfaction, how can they settle the Central Realm?
translations.idiomatic: "The rebels plunder gold, silk, and captives and send everything to Fanyang; once they have their fill, how can they hold the Central Plain?

sentences.zh: 華人為之用者，獨周摯、高尚等數人，餘皆脅制偷合，至天下大計，非所知也。

translations.literal: Of Chinese serving them, only Zhou Zhi, Gao Shang, and a few others; the rest are all coerced and steal union—as for the great plan of the realm, that is not what they know.
translations.idiomatic: Only a few Chinese such as Zhou Zhi and Gao Shang truly serve them; the rest are coerced opportunists who know nothing of governing the realm.

sentences.zh: 不出二年，無寇矣，陛下無欲速。

translations.literal: Within two years there will be no bandits; Your Majesty should not desire speed.
translations.idiomatic: Within two years the rebels will be gone; Your Majesty must not hurry.

sentences.zh: 夫王者之師，當務萬全，圖久安，使無後害。

translations.literal: The army of a true king should strive for complete security, plan long peace, and leave no later harm.
translations.idiomatic: A true king's army must seek complete security, plan for lasting peace, and leave no later trouble.

sentences.zh: 今詔李光弼守太原，出井陘，郭子儀取馮翊，入河東，則史思明、張忠志不敢離范陽、常山，安守忠、田乾真不敢離長安，是以三地禁其四將也。

translations.literal: Now order Li Guangbi to guard Taiyuan and issue from Jingxing Pass, Guo Ziyi to take Fengyi and enter Hedong—then Shi Siming and Zhang Zhongzhi will not dare leave Fanyang and Changshan, An Shouzhong and Tian Qianzhen will not dare leave Chang'an; thus three places will confine their four generals.
translations.idiomatic: Order Li Guangbi to hold Taiyuan and advance through Jingxing Pass, Guo Ziyi to take Fengyi and enter Hedong—then Shi Siming and Zhang Zhongzhi will not dare leave Fanyang and Changshan, An Shouzhong and Tian Qianzhen will not dare leave Chang'an; three positions will pin down their four generals.

sentences.zh: 隨祿山者，獨阿史那承慶耳。

translations.literal: Of those who followed Lushan, only Ashina Chengqing.
translations.idiomatic: Of those who truly followed Lushan of their own will, only Ashina Chengqing.

sentences.zh: 使子儀毋取華，令賊得通關中，則北守范陽，西救長安，奔命數千里，其精卒勁騎，不逾年而弊。

translations.literal: Have Ziyi not take Huazhou; let the rebels pass through to Guanzhong—then they will guard Fanyang in the north and rescue Chang'an in the west, racing on urgent orders for thousands of li; their elite troops and strong cavalry will wear out within a year.
translations.idiomatic: Have Guo Ziyi hold back from taking Huazhou and let the rebels break through into Guanzhong—they will then hold Fanyang in the north while rushing west to save Chang'an, racing thousands of li on desperate orders until their best troops and horses are spent within a year.

sentences.zh: 我常以逸待勞，來避其鋒，去翦其疲，以所征之兵會撫風，與太原、朔方軍互擊之。

translations.literal: We always use rest to await fatigue—when they come, avoid their edge; when they leave, cut down their exhaustion; with the recruited troops meet at Fufeng and with the Taiyuan and Shuofang armies strike them in turn.
translations.idiomatic: We should always fight rested against their weariness—evade their thrust when they advance, strike their exhausted ranks when they withdraw, and with our mobilized forces join at Fufeng to hit them in rotation with the Taiyuan and Shuofang armies.

sentences.zh: 徐命建甯王為范陽節度大使，北並塞與光弼相掎角，以取范陽。

translations.literal: Gradually appoint the Prince of Jianning as Fanyang military commissioner; north along the frontier pincer with Guangbi to take Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Then gradually appoint the Prince of Jianning as military commissioner of Fanyang, advance north along the frontier in a pincer with Li Guangbi, and seize Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 賊失巢窟，當死河南諸將手。」

translations.literal: When the rebels lose their nest and lair, they will die at the hands of the generals south of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Once the rebels lose their base, the generals south of the Yellow River will finish them off.

sentences.zh: 帝然之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 會西方兵大集，帝欲速得長安，曰：「今戰必勝，攻必取，何暇千里先事范陽乎？」

translations.literal: Just then western troops greatly assembled; the Emperor wished to recover Chang'an quickly and said: "Now in battle we are sure to win, in attack sure to take—what leisure to deal with Fanyang a thousand li away first?
translations.idiomatic: Just then troops from the west massed in great numbers, and the Emperor, eager to retake Chang'an quickly, said, "We are sure to win every battle and take every city we assault—why waste time on Fanyang a thousand li away?

sentences.zh: 泌曰：「必得兩京，則賊再強，我再困。

translations.literal: Bi said: "If we must recover both capitals, then the rebels will grow strong again and we will be exhausted again.
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "If we insist on recovering both capitals first, the rebels will regroup and grow strong again while we exhaust ourselves once more.

sentences.zh: 且我所恃者，磧西突騎、西北諸戎耳。

translations.literal: Moreover what we rely on are the Western Desert Turkic cavalry and the various northwestern tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, what we depend on are the Turkic horsemen west of the deserts and the various tribal allies of the northwest.

sentences.zh: 若先取京師，期必在春，關東早熱，馬且病，士皆思歸，不可以戰。

translations.literal: If we first take the capital, the deadline must fall in spring; east of the pass grows hot early—the horses will sicken and the men all think of returning home—they cannot fight.
translations.idiomatic: If we strike for the capital first, we must finish by spring—but the lands east of the pass turn hot early, the horses will fall ill, and the men will all long for home; they will not be fit to fight.

sentences.zh: 賊得休士養徒，必復來南。

translations.literal: The rebels will rest their troops and regroup—they will surely come south again.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels will rest and rebuild their forces, then march south again.

sentences.zh: 此危道也。」

translations.literal: This is a perilous course."
translations.idiomatic: That is a dangerous path."

sentences.zh: 帝不聽。

translations.literal: The Emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor refused to heed him.

sentences.zh: 二京平，帝奉迎上皇，自請歸東宮以遂子道。

translations.literal: When both capitals were pacified, the Emperor went to welcome the Retired Emperor and himself requested to return to the Eastern Palace to fulfill filial duty as son.
translations.idiomatic: After both capitals were recovered, the Emperor went to welcome the Retired Emperor and asked to move back to the Eastern Palace so he could properly fulfill his duties as a son.

sentences.zh: 泌曰：「上皇不來矣。

translations.literal: Bi said: "The Retired Emperor will not come.
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "The Retired Emperor will not come.

sentences.zh: 人臣尚七十而傳，況欲勞上皇以天下事乎。」

translations.literal: Even ministers at seventy transfer office—how much more should one burden the Retired Emperor with affairs of the realm?
translations.idiomatic: Even ordinary officials retire at seventy—how can we expect the Retired Emperor to bear the burden of governing the realm?

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「奈何？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "What then shall we do?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "What can be done?"

sentences.zh: 泌乃為群臣通奏，具言天子思戀晨昏，請促還以就孝養。

translations.literal: Bi then drafted a memorial on behalf of the officials, fully stating the Son of Heaven's longing morning and evening, requesting he be urged to return for filial nurture.
translations.idiomatic: Bi then drafted a memorial on behalf of the court officials, describing at length the Son of Heaven's longing for his father day and night and asking that the Retired Emperor be urged to return so his son could care for him in filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 上皇得初奏，答曰：「當與我劍南一道自奉，不復東矣。」

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor received the first memorial and replied: "Give me Jiannan circuit for my own support—I will not return east again.
translations.idiomatic: When the Retired Emperor received the first memorial, he replied, "Grant me Jiannan circuit to support myself in retirement—I will not come east again.

sentences.zh: 帝甚憂。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly worried.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 及再奏至，喜曰：「吾方得為天子父！」

translations.literal: When the second memorial arrived, he said joyfully: "I can finally be the Father of Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: When the second memorial arrived, he said with delight, "At last I can be the father of the Son of Heaven!

sentences.zh: 遂下誥戒行。

translations.literal: Thereupon he issued an edict enjoining departure.
translations.idiomatic: He then issued an edict ordering his return.

sentences.zh: 崔圓、李輔國以泌親信，疾之。

translations.literal: Cui Yuan and Li Fuguo, because Bi was close and trusted, resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuan and Li Fuguo resented Bi because he enjoyed the Emperor's close trust.

sentences.zh: 泌畏禍，願隱衡山。

translations.literal: Bi feared harm and wished to retire to Mount Heng.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing reprisals, Bi asked to withdraw and live in seclusion on Mount Heng.

sentences.zh: 有詔給三品祿，賜隱士服，為治室廬。

translations.literal: An edict granted third-rank stipend, bestowed recluse's garb, and built him a dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted him third-rank stipend, gave him the garb of a recluse, and had a residence built for him.

sentences.zh: 泌嘗取松樛枝以隱背，名曰「養和」，後得如龍形者，因以獻帝，四方爭效之。

translations.literal: Bi once took a bent pine branch to lean his back on, calling it "Nourishing Harmony"; later obtaining one shaped like a dragon, he presented it to the Emperor—and everywhere people rushed to imitate it.
translations.idiomatic: Bi once used a bent pine branch to support his back and called it "Nourishing Harmony." When he later found one shaped like a dragon and presented it to the Emperor, people everywhere rushed to copy the fashion.

sentences.zh: 代宗立，召至，舍蓬萊殿書閣。

translations.literal: When Daizong acceded, he summoned Bi and lodged him in the library pavilion of Penglai Hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daizong took the throne, he summoned Bi and housed him in the library pavilion of Penglai Hall.

sentences.zh: 初，泌無妻，不食肉，帝乃賜光福裏第，強詔食肉，為娶朔方故留後李暐甥，昏日，敕北軍供帳。

translations.literal: At first Bi had no wife and ate no meat; the Emperor then granted a mansion in Guangfu Lane, compelled him by edict to eat meat, and married him to a niece of Li Wei, former Shuofang deputy—on the wedding day he ordered the northern army to provide ceremonial equipment.
translations.idiomatic: At first Bi had no wife and abstained from meat, so the Emperor granted him a mansion in Guangfu Lane, ordered him by edict to eat meat, and arranged his marriage to a niece of Li Wei, the former deputy military governor of Shuofang; on the wedding day he commanded the northern army to supply the ceremonial furnishings.

sentences.zh: 元載惡不附己，因江西觀察使魏少遊請僚佐，載稱泌才，以試秘書少監充判官。

translations.literal: Yuan Zai hated those who would not attach to him; when Jiangxi observation commissioner Wei Shaoyou requested staff, Zai praised Bi's talent and had him serve as provisional secretary director as administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai disliked anyone who would not align with him. When the Jiangxi observation commissioner Wei Shaoyou asked for staff, Zai praised Bi's ability and had him appointed provisional secretary director to serve as Wei's administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 載誅，帝召還。

translations.literal: When Zai was executed, the Emperor summoned him back.
translations.idiomatic: After Zai was executed, the Emperor recalled Bi to court.

sentences.zh: 復為常袞所忌，出為楚州刺史，辭不行，帝亦留之。

translations.literal: Again envied by Chang Gun, he was sent out as prefect of Chuzhou; he declined and would not go, and the Emperor also kept him.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Gun envied him again and had him appointed prefect of Chuzhou, but Bi declined the post and refused to leave; the Emperor kept him at court as well.

sentences.zh: 會澧州缺，袞盛言南方凋瘵，請輟泌治之，乃授澧、朗、峽團練使，徙杭州刺史，皆有風績。

translations.literal: When Lizhou fell vacant, Gun strongly described the south's devastation and asked that Bi be spared to govern it; he was made regimental commissioner of Li, Lang, and Xia, then transferred to prefect of Hangzhou—in all he had fine administrative record.
translations.idiomatic: When Lizhou fell vacant, Gun spoke at length of the south's ruin and asked that Bi be sent to govern it; Bi was made regimental commissioner of Li, Lang, and Xia, then transferred to prefect of Hangzhou, and in every post he left a record of fine governance.

sentences.zh: 德宗在奉天，召赴行在，授左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Dezong was at Fengtian, he summoned Bi to the mobile court and appointed him Left Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong was at Fengtian, he summoned Bi to the mobile court and appointed him Left Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 時李懷光叛，歲又蝗旱，議者欲赦懷光。

translations.literal: At the time Li Huai'guang rebelled and the year also saw locusts and drought; discussants wished to pardon Huai'guang.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Huai'guang had rebelled, and the year also brought locusts and drought; some at court argued that he should be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 帝博問群臣，泌破一桐葉附使以進，曰：「陛下與懷光，君臣之分不可復合，如此葉矣。」

translations.literal: The Emperor broadly questioned the officials; Bi tore a paulownia leaf and had the messenger bring it in, saying: "Your Majesty and Huai'guang—monarch and minister—the bond cannot be mended again, like this leaf.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked the officials broadly for their views; Bi tore a paulownia leaf in two and sent it in with the messenger, saying, "Your Majesty and Huai'guang—the bond between sovereign and subject cannot be mended, just like this leaf.

sentences.zh: 由是不赦。

translations.literal: Because of this he was not pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, Huai'guang was not pardoned.

sentences.zh: 始，朱泚亂，帝約吐蕃赴援，賂以安西、北庭。

translations.literal: At the start, when Zhu Ci rebelled, the Emperor promised Tibet aid and bribed them with Anxi and Beiting.
