translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhu Ci rebelled, the Emperor had promised Tibetan aid and offered Anxi and Beiting as reward.

sentences.zh: 既而渾瑊與賊戰咸陽，泚大敗，吐蕃以師追北不甚力，因大掠武功而歸。

translations.literal: Soon after Hun Jian fought the rebels at Xianyang and Ci was greatly defeated; Tibet pursued northward without much effort and instead greatly plundered Wugong and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Hun Jian fought the rebels at Xianyang and Zhu Ci was routed; the Tibetans pursued northward halfheartedly and instead looted Wugong on a grand scale before withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 京師平，來請如約。

translations.literal: When the capital was pacified, they came to request fulfillment of the agreement.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was recovered, the Tibetans came to demand the territories promised them.

sentences.zh: 帝業許，欲遂與之。

translations.literal: The Emperor had already agreed and wished to give them the territories.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had already agreed and intended to hand the territories over.

sentences.zh: 泌曰：「安西、北庭，控制西域五十七國及十姓突厥，皆悍兵處，以分吐蕃勢，使不得並兵東侵。

translations.literal: Bi said: "Anxi and Beiting control the fifty-seven states of the Western Regions and the Ten Surname Turks—all places of fierce warriors—to divide Tibet's power and keep them from combining armies to invade east.
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "Anxi and Beiting hold sway over the fifty-seven states of the Western Regions and the Ten Surname Turks—lands of fierce warriors that split Tibetan strength and keep them from massing their armies for an eastern invasion.

sentences.zh: 今與其地，則關中危矣。

translations.literal: If we now give them those lands, Guanzhong will be in peril.
translations.idiomatic: If we surrender those territories now, Guanzhong will be in grave danger.

sentences.zh: 且吐蕃向持兩端不戰，又掠我武功，乃賊也，奈何與之？」

translations.literal: Moreover Tibet has held two sides and not fought, yet plundered our Wugong—they are bandits; how can we give them territory?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the Tibetans sat on the fence and refused to fight, then plundered our Wugong—they acted as bandits; how can we reward them with territory?

sentences.zh: 遂止。

translations.literal: Thereupon he stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor thereupon abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，拜陝虢觀察使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan, he was appointed observation commissioner of Shan and Guo.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Zhenyuan era, he was appointed observation commissioner of Shan and Guo.

sentences.zh: 泌始鑿山開車道至三門，以便饟漕。

translations.literal: Bi first cut through mountains to open a cart road to Sanmen to facilitate grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Bi was the first to cut through the mountains and open a cart road to Sanmen to ease the transport of grain supplies.

sentences.zh: 以勞，進檢校禮部尚書。

translations.literal: For his labor he was promoted to Acting Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of this labor, he was promoted to Acting Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 淮西兵防秋屯鄜州，已而四千人亡歸，或曰吳少誠密招之。

translations.literal: Huainan-west troops garrisoned for autumn defense at Binzhou; soon four thousand deserted and returned—some said Wu Shaocheng secretly recruited them.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan-west troops stationed at Binzhou for autumn defense soon saw four thousand men desert and flee homeward; some said Wu Shaocheng had secretly recruited them.

sentences.zh: 既入境，泌邀險悉擊殺之。

translations.literal: Once they entered the jurisdiction, Bi ambushed them at narrow passes and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Once they entered his jurisdiction, Bi ambushed them at narrow passes and killed them to the last man.

sentences.zh: 三年，拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，累封鄴縣侯。

translations.literal: In the third year he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Fellow of the Secretariat and Chancellery, cumulatively enfeoffed as Marquis of Ye County.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor, and was cumulatively enfeoffed as Marquis of Ye County.

sentences.zh: 初，張延賞減天下吏員，人情愁怨，至流離死道路者。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhang Yanshang had reduced officials empire-wide; popular sentiment was resentful and aggrieved—to the point of wanderers dying on the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhang Yanshang had cut official posts across the empire; public resentment ran so deep that people were driven from their homes and died along the roads.

sentences.zh: 泌請復之，帝未從，因問：「今戶口減承平時幾何？」

translations.literal: Bi requested restoration; the Emperor did not agree and asked: "How much has the population declined from peacetime?
translations.idiomatic: Bi asked that the quotas be restored, but the Emperor refused and asked, "By how much has the population fallen since peacetime?

sentences.zh: 曰：「三之二。」

translations.literal: He replied: "By two-thirds."
translations.idiomatic: Bi replied, "By two-thirds."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「人既雕耗，員何可復？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Since the people are already depleted, how can the quotas be restored?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "If the population has already been so depleted, how can we restore the quotas?"

sentences.zh: 泌曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Bi said: "That is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "That is not so.

sentences.zh: 戶口雖耗，而事多承平十倍。

translations.literal: Though the population is depleted, affairs are ten times those of peacetime.
translations.idiomatic: Though the population has shrunk, the volume of business is ten times what it was in peacetime.

sentences.zh: 陛下欲省州縣則可，而吏員不可減。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty wishes to streamline prefectures and counties, that is possible—but official quotas cannot be cut.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty may consolidate prefectures and counties if you wish, but the number of officials cannot be reduced.

sentences.zh: 今州或參軍署券，縣佐史判案。

translations.literal: Now at prefectures military aides sometimes sign documents; at counties clerks sometimes judge cases.
translations.idiomatic: Today at some prefectures military aides sign official documents, and at some counties clerical assistants decide cases.

sentences.zh: 所謂省官者，去其冗員，非常員也。」

translations.literal: What is called reducing officials means removing redundant posts—not regular posts."
translations.idiomatic: What people call cutting officials should mean removing redundant posts, not eliminating regular ones."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「若何為冗員？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "What then are redundant posts?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked, "What counts as a redundant post?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「州參軍無職事及兼、試額內官者。

translations.literal: He replied: "Prefectural military aides without duties, and concurrent and provisional posts within the quota.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Prefectural military aides with no real duties, and concurrent or provisional posts counted within the regular quota.

sentences.zh: 兼、試，自至德以來有之，比正員三之一，可悉罷。」

translations.literal: Concurrent and provisional posts have existed since the Zhide era—about one-third of regular posts—all can be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: Concurrent and provisional appointments have existed since the Zhide era and now make up about one-third of regular posts; all of them can be abolished."

sentences.zh: 帝乃許復吏員，而罷冗官。

translations.literal: The Emperor then agreed to restore official quotas and abolish redundant posts.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then agreed to restore official quotas while abolishing redundant posts.

sentences.zh: 泌又條奏：「中朝官常侍、賓客十員，其六員可罷；

translations.literal: Bi also submitted a detailed memorial: "Of the ten Central Court attendant and guest posts, six can be abolished;
translations.idiomatic: Bi also submitted a detailed memorial: "Of the ten attendant and guest posts at the central court, six can be abolished;

sentences.zh: 左右贊善三十員，其二十員可罷。

translations.literal: Of the thirty Left and Right Supporters of Goodness, twenty can be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Of the thirty Left and Right Supporters of Goodness, twenty can be abolished.

sentences.zh: 如舊制，諸王未出閤，官屬皆不除。

translations.literal: Under the old system, when princes had not left the inner apartments, no staff posts were filled.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, when princes had not yet left the inner quarters, none of their staff posts were filled.

sentences.zh: 而所收科奉，乃多於減員矣。」

translations.literal: Yet the stipends saved would still exceed what had been cut.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the savings in stipends would still exceed the posts eliminated.

sentences.zh: 帝悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 是時，州刺史月奉至千緡，方鎮所取無藝，而京官祿寡薄，自方鎮入八座，至謂罷權。

translations.literal: At this time prefects' monthly salaries reached a thousand strings; military governors took without limit, while capital officials' salaries were meager—those who went from governorships to the Eight Chief Offices even called it losing power.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a prefect's monthly salary could reach a thousand strings, military governors extracted revenue without restraint, and capital officials were paid poorly; men who moved from a governorship into the Eight Chief Offices even spoke of it as surrendering real power.

sentences.zh: 薛邕由左丞貶歙州刺史，家人恨降之晚。

translations.literal: Xue Yong was demoted from Left Vice Director to prefect of Shezhou; his family resented that the demotion came so late.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yong was demoted from Left Vice Director to prefect of Shezhou, and his family complained that the appointment had come too late.

sentences.zh: 崔祐甫任吏部員外，求為洪州別駕。

translations.literal: Cui Youfu served as Vice Director of Personnel and sought to be vice-prefect of Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Youfu, while serving as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, asked to be appointed vice-prefect of Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 使府賓佐有所忤者，薦為郎官。

translations.literal: Those who offended their governor's staff were recommended for ministerial posts.
translations.idiomatic: Staff members who had offended their governor were recommended for posts in the capital ministries.

sentences.zh: 其當遷台閣者，皆以不赴取罪去。

translations.literal: Those who ought to be promoted to the capital offices all took blame for refusing and left.
translations.idiomatic: Those who ought to have been promoted to the central ministries were punished and dismissed for refusing to leave their provincial posts.

sentences.zh: 泌以為外太重，內太輕，乃請隨官閑劇，普增其奉，時以為宜。

translations.literal: Bi considered the outer too heavy and the inner too light; he requested that stipends be broadly increased according to each post's busyness, and the time judged it fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Bi believed that provincial posts were overpaid and capital posts underpaid, and asked that salaries be raised broadly according to each office's workload; people at the time thought this reasonable.

sentences.zh: 而竇參多沮亂其事，不能悉如所請。

translations.literal: But Dou Can largely obstructed the matter so it could not all be done as requested.
translations.idiomatic: But Dou Can obstructed the plan in many ways, so not all of Bi's requests could be carried out.

sentences.zh: 泌又白罷拾遺、補闕，帝雖不從，然因是不除諫官，唯用韓皋、歸登。

translations.literal: Bi also urged abolishing remonstrance and rectification posts; though the Emperor did not agree, from this he did not fill remonstrance posts—only employing Han Gao and Gui Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Bi also urged abolishing the remonstrance and rectification posts; though the Emperor did not agree, from then on he stopped appointing remonstrance officials and employed only Han Gao and Gui Deng.

sentences.zh: 泌因收其公廨錢，令二人寓食中書舍人署。

translations.literal: Bi then collected their office funds and had the two lodge and eat at the Secretariat drafters' office.
translations.idiomatic: Bi then took their office funds and had the two men lodge and take meals at the Secretariat drafters' office.

sentences.zh: 凡三年，始以韋綬、梁肅為左右補闕。

translations.literal: After three years altogether, Wei Shou and Liang Su were first appointed Left and Right Rectification Censors.
translations.idiomatic: Only after three years were Wei Shou and Liang Su finally appointed Left and Right Rectification Censors.

sentences.zh: 太子妃蕭母，郜國公主也，坐蠱媚，幽禁中，帝怒，責太子，太子不知所對。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince's consort's mother, the Princess of Guo, was convicted of witchcraft and seduction, imprisoned within the palace; the Emperor was angry, rebuked the Crown Prince, and the Crown Prince did not know how to reply.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince's consort was surnamed Xiao; her mother was the Princess of Guo, who was convicted of witchcraft and seduction and imprisoned within the palace. The Emperor was furious and rebuked the Crown Prince, who did not know how to answer.

sentences.zh: 泌入，帝數稱舒王賢，泌揣帝有廢立意，因曰：「陛下有一子而疑之，乃欲立弟之子，臣不敢以古事爭。

translations.literal: Bi entered; the Emperor repeatedly praised Prince Shu as worthy; Bi surmised the Emperor had intent to depose and said: "Your Majesty has one son yet doubts him, and would instead establish your younger brother's son—I dare not argue from ancient precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Bi entered, the Emperor repeatedly praised Prince Shu as worthy. Sensing that the Emperor meant to depose the heir, Bi said, "Your Majesty has one son yet doubt him, and would instead install your younger brother's son—I dare not argue from ancient examples.

sentences.zh: 且十宅諸叔，陛下奉之若何？」

translations.literal: Moreover the various uncles of the Ten Mansions—how would Your Majesty treat them?
translations.idiomatic: And the many uncles of the Ten Mansions—how would Your Majesty treat them all?

sentences.zh: 帝赫然曰：「卿何知舒王非朕子？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said sharply: "How do you know Prince Shu is not my son?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said sharply, "How do you know Prince Shu is not my son?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下昔為臣言之。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your Majesty once told me as much.
translations.idiomatic: Bi replied, "Your Majesty once told me so yourself.

sentences.zh: 陛下有嫡子以為疑，弟之子敢自信于陛下乎？」

translations.literal: Your Majesty doubts your own eldest son—would a younger brother's son dare trust himself before Your Majesty?"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty doubts your own eldest son, would a nephew dare trust that he enjoys your full confidence?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿違朕意，不顧家族邪？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "You defy my intent—do you not care for your clan?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "You defy my wishes—do you not care what becomes of your family?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣衰老，位宰相，以諫而誅，分也。

translations.literal: He replied: "I am old and decrepit, holding the post of chancellor—to be executed for remonstrance is my lot.
translations.idiomatic: Bi replied, "I am old and frail, and I hold the post of chancellor; if I am executed for remonstrance, that is my proper lot.

sentences.zh: 使太子廢，它日陛下悔曰『我惟一子殺之，泌不吾諫，吾亦殺爾子』，則臣絕祀矣。

translations.literal: If the Crown Prince is deposed, someday Your Majesty may regret and say 'I killed my only son, and Bi did not remonstrate—I will kill your son too'—then my line ends.
translations.idiomatic: If the Crown Prince is deposed, someday Your Majesty may regret and say, 'I killed my only son, and Bi never remonstrated with me—I will kill your son too'—and then my line will end.

sentences.zh: 雖有兄弟子，非所歆也。」

translations.literal: Though you have a brother's son, that is not what one would cherish."
translations.idiomatic: Even if you have a brother's son, that is not the heir one would truly cherish."

sentences.zh: 即噫嗚流涕。

translations.literal: He immediately sobbed and wept.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately broke into sobs and wept.

sentences.zh: 因稱：「昔太宗詔：『太子不道，籓王窺伺者，兩廢之。』

translations.literal: He then cited: "Formerly Emperor Taizong decreed: 'If the Crown Prince is unprincipled and a feudal prince watches and waits, both are to be deposed.
translations.idiomatic: He then cited Emperor Taizong's decree: "If the Crown Prince is unprincipled and a feudal prince watches and waits, both are to be deposed.

sentences.zh: 陛下疑東宮而稱舒王賢，得無窺伺乎？

translations.literal: Your Majesty doubts the Eastern Palace yet praises Prince Shu as worthy—is that not watching and waiting?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty doubt the Eastern Palace yet praise Prince Shu as worthy—is that not the behavior of one watching and waiting?

sentences.zh: 若太子得罪，請亦廢之而立皇孫，千秋萬歲後，天下猶陛下子孫有也。

translations.literal: If the Crown Prince is guilty, please also depose him and establish the imperial grandson—ten thousand years hence the realm will still have Your Majesty's descendants.
translations.idiomatic: If the Crown Prince is guilty, depose him and install the imperial grandson instead—ten thousand years from now the realm will still belong to Your Majesty's line.

sentences.zh: 且郜國為其女妒忌，而蠱惑東宮，豈可以妻母累太子乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover the Princess of Guo was jealous on her daughter's behalf and bewitched the Eastern Palace—how can the Crown Prince be implicated for his consort's mother?'
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the Princess of Guo acted out of jealousy for her daughter and used witchcraft to influence the Eastern Palace—how can the Crown Prince be punished for his consort's mother?

sentences.zh: 執爭數十，意益堅，帝寤，太子乃得安。

translations.literal: He argued passionately dozens of times, his resolve growing firmer; the Emperor came to his senses and the Crown Prince was secured.
translations.idiomatic: He argued passionately for a long time, his resolve growing firmer; the Emperor came to his senses, and the Crown Prince was spared.

sentences.zh: 初，興元後國用大屈，封物皆三損二。

translations.literal: Initially, after Xingyuan the state finances were greatly strained—all enfeoffment goods were reduced by two-thirds.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after the court's withdrawal to Xingyuan, state finances were severely strained and all enfeoffment allotments were cut by two-thirds.

sentences.zh: 舊制，堂封歲三千六百縑，後才千二百。

translations.literal: Under the old system, hall enfeoffment was thirty-six hundred bolts of silk yearly; afterward only twelve hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, hall enfeoffment came to thirty-six hundred bolts of silk each year; afterward it was reduced to only twelve hundred.

sentences.zh: 至是，帝使還舊封。

translations.literal: At this time the Emperor had the old enfeoffment restored.
translations.idiomatic: At this point the Emperor ordered the old enfeoffment allotments restored.

sentences.zh: 於是李晟、馬燧、渾瑊各食實封，悉讓送泌，泌不納。

translations.literal: Thereupon Li Sheng, Ma Sui, and Hun Jian each drew real enfeoffment income and all sent their shares to Bi—Bi would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Li Sheng, Ma Sui, and Hun Jian, each drawing income from real enfeoffments, sent their shares to Bi, but Bi refused to accept them.

sentences.zh: 時方鎮私獻於帝，歲凡五十萬緡，其後稍損至三十萬，帝以用度乏問泌，泌請：「天下供錢歲百萬給宮中，勸不受私獻。

translations.literal: At the time military governors privately presented to the Emperor yearly about five hundred thousand strings; later this gradually fell to three hundred thousand; the Emperor asked Bi because expenses were insufficient; Bi requested: "Let the empire's tribute money be a million yearly for the palace—I urge that private gifts not be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: At the time military governors privately presented the Emperor with about five hundred thousand strings each year; later this gradually fell to three hundred thousand. Because expenses were insufficient, the Emperor asked Bi, who proposed: "Let the empire's tribute revenue of one million strings each year supply the palace, and I urge that private gifts no longer be accepted.

sentences.zh: 凡詔旨須索，即代兩稅，則方鎮可以行法，天下紓矣。」

translations.literal: Whenever edicts require supplies, substitute the two taxes—then military governors can enforce the law and the realm will be relieved."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court needs supplies by edict, pay for them through the two-tax system instead; then military governors can enforce the law properly and the burden on the realm will be eased."

sentences.zh: 帝嘗從容言：「盧杞清介敢言，然少學，不能廣朕以古道，人皆指其奸而朕不覺也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor once said at ease: "Lu Qi is upright and outspoken, yet he lacks learning and cannot broaden Me with the ways of antiquity. Everyone points to his treachery, yet I do not perceive it."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once remarked in an unhurried tone: "Lu Qi is incorruptible and bold in speech, yet he is poorly educated and cannot broaden my understanding with the ways of antiquity. Everyone calls him treacherous, but I do not see it.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下能覺杞之惡，安致建中禍邪？

translations.literal: Bi replied: "If Your Majesty could perceive Qi's wickedness, how would the disasters of the Jianzhong era have come about?
translations.idiomatic: Bi replied: "If Your Majesty had been able to see Qi's wickedness, how could the catastrophes of the Jianzhong era have occurred?

sentences.zh: 李揆和蕃，顏真卿使希烈，其害舊德多矣。

translations.literal: Li Kui made peace with the Tibetans; Yan Zhenqing was sent to Xi Lie—the harm done to venerable ministers was great indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kui made peace with the Tibetans, and Yan Zhenqing was dispatched to Li Xilie; the injury inflicted on esteemed old ministers was immense.

sentences.zh: 又楊炎罪不至死，杞擠陷之而相關播。

translations.literal: Moreover, Yang Yan's offense did not warrant death, yet Qi squeezed him out and ruined him, then made Guan Bo chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Yang Yan's crimes did not merit death, yet Qi forced him out and framed him, and afterward installed Guan Bo as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 懷光立功，逼使其叛。

translations.literal: Huai Guang had rendered meritorious service; Qi drove him until he rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Huai'guang had won great merit, yet Qi hounded him until he turned rebel.

sentences.zh: 此欺天也。」

translations.literal: This was deceiving Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: This was nothing less than deceiving Heaven itself."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿言誠有之。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "What you say is indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "What you say is indeed true.

sentences.zh: 然楊炎視朕如三尺童子，有所論奏，可則退，不許則辭官，非特杞惡之也。

translations.literal: Yet Yang Yan treated Me like a child of three feet—when he submitted recommendations, if approved he withdrew; if refused he resigned. It was not Qi alone who hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yang Yan treated me like a small child: when he submitted a proposal, he withdrew if I approved it and resigned if I did not. It was not only Qi who despised him.

sentences.zh: 且建中亂，卿亦知桑道茂語乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, regarding the Jianzhong turmoil—do you also know what Sang Daomao said?
translations.idiomatic: And as for the chaos of the Jianzhong era—do you also know what Sang Daomao said?

sentences.zh: 乃命當然。」

translations.literal: It was simply fate taking its course."
translations.idiomatic: It was simply destiny unfolding as it must."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「夫命者，已然之言。

translations.literal: Bi replied: "As for fate—it is merely words about what has already come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: Bi replied: "Fate is simply language applied to what has already happened.

sentences.zh: 主相造命，不當言命。

translations.literal: The ruler and ministers create destiny; they ought not speak of fate.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign and his ministers shape destiny themselves; they should not speak of fate.

sentences.zh: 言命，則不復賞善罰惡矣。

translations.literal: If one speaks of fate, one no longer rewards good and punishes evil.
translations.idiomatic: Once one invokes fate, one no longer rewards virtue and punishes wickedness.

sentences.zh: 桀曰：『我生不有命自天。』

translations.literal: Jie said: 'From birth I have had a mandate from Heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: Jie said, 'From birth I have possessed a mandate from Heaven.'

sentences.zh: 武王數紂曰：『謂己有天命。』

translations.literal: King Wu reproached Zhou saying: 'He claims Heaven's mandate for himself.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu rebuked Zhou, saying, 'He claims Heaven's mandate for himself.'

sentences.zh: 君而言命，則桀、紂矣。」

translations.literal: When a ruler speaks of fate, he becomes Jie and Zhou."
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler talks of fate, he becomes another Jie or Zhou."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕請不復言命。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I shall speak of fate no more."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "I shall speak of fate no more."

sentences.zh: 俄加集賢殿、崇文館大學士，修國史。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was made Grand Academician of the Jixian Hall and Chongwen Library, with charge of compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed Grand Academician of the Jixian Hall and Chongwen Library, with responsibility for compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 泌建言：學士加大，始中宗時，及張說為之，固辭，乃以學士知院事。

translations.literal: Bi submitted a memorial: the elevation of academicians to 'Grand' began in Emperor Zhongzong's reign; when Zhang Yue held the post he firmly declined and served only as academician in charge of the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Bi submitted a memorial noting that the title of Grand Academician dated from Emperor Zhongzong's reign; when Zhang Yue received it he firmly declined and served only as academician in charge of the institute.

sentences.zh: 至崔圓復為大學士，亦引泌為讓而止。

translations.literal: When Cui Yuan again became Grand Academician, he cited Bi's precedent and likewise declined.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Yuan was again made Grand Academician, he cited Bi's example and likewise declined the grand title.

sentences.zh: 帝以「前世上巳、九日，皆大宴集，而寒食多與上巳同時，欲以三月名節，自我為古，若何而可？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "In former ages the Shangsi and Double-Ninth festivals were both occasions for grand banquets, yet Cold Food often coincided with Shangsi. I wish to establish a named festival in the third month, making something new from antiquity—how might this be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "In earlier times the Shangsi and Double-Ninth festivals were both celebrated with great banquets, yet Cold Food often fell at the same time as Shangsi. I wish to establish a named festival in the third month, creating a new custom in the spirit of antiquity—how might this be accomplished?

sentences.zh: 泌請：「廢正月晦，以二月朔為中和節，因賜大臣戚裏尺，謂之裁度。

translations.literal: Bi proposed: "Abolish the last day of the first month and make the first day of the second month the Festival of Central Harmony. Present ministers and imperial kin with a one-foot ruler, called a measurement.
translations.idiomatic: Bi proposed: "Abolish the last day of the first month and make the first day of the second month the Festival of Central Harmony. Give ministers and imperial relatives a one-foot ruler as a gift, called a caidu, or measurement.

sentences.zh: 民間以青囊盛百穀瓜果種相問遺，號為獻生子。

translations.literal: Among the people, green pouches filled with seeds of all grains, fruits, and melons would be exchanged as gifts, called 'offering the birth of life.'
translations.idiomatic: Among the people, green pouches filled with seeds of every grain, fruit, and melon would be exchanged as gifts, an observance known as 'offering the birth of life.'

sentences.zh: 里閭釀宜春酒，以祭勾芒神，祈豐年。

translations.literal: In neighborhoods they would brew Yichun wine to sacrifice to the god Gou Mang and pray for a bountiful year.
translations.idiomatic: In every neighborhood they would brew Yichun wine to sacrifice to the god Gou Mang and pray for an abundant harvest.

sentences.zh: 百官進農書，以示務本。」

translations.literal: All officials would submit treatises on agriculture to show devotion to fundamental pursuits."
translations.idiomatic: All officials would submit treatises on agriculture to demonstrate their commitment to fundamental pursuits."

sentences.zh: 帝悅，乃著令，與上巳、九日為三令節，中外皆賜緡錢燕會。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased and issued an edict making it, together with Shangsi and the Double-Ninth, one of three statutory festivals; within and without the court all received strings of cash for banquets.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was pleased and issued an edict establishing it, together with Shangsi and the Double-Ninth, as one of three statutory festivals; inside and outside the court all received strings of cash for banquets.

sentences.zh: 四年八月，月蝕東壁，泌曰：「東壁，圖書府，大臣當有憂者。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year, the moon eclipsed Dongbi. Bi said: "Dongbi is the asterism of the library—some great minister should suffer misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fourth year, the moon eclipsed Dongbi. Bi said: "Dongbi is the asterism of the library—a great minister should suffer misfortune.

sentences.zh: 吾以宰相兼學士，當之矣。

translations.literal: As chancellor who also holds the academician post, I should be the one.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor who also holds the academician post, I should be the one to bear it.

sentences.zh: 昔燕國公張說由是以亡，又可免乎？」

translations.literal: Formerly Duke of Yan Zhang Yue perished on this account—can one escape it?"
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the Duke of Yan, Zhang Yue, died on account of this very omen—can one escape it?

sentences.zh: 明年果卒，年六十八，贈太子太傅。

translations.literal: The next year he indeed died, at age sixty-eight; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he did indeed die, at the age of sixty-eight, and was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 泌出入中禁，事四君，數為權幸所疾，常以智免。

translations.literal: Bi entered and left the inner palace, serving four sovereigns; he was repeatedly resented by the powerful and favored, yet usually escaped harm through wit.
translations.idiomatic: Bi moved in and out of the inner palace, serving four sovereigns; he was repeatedly envied and hated by the powerful and favored, yet usually preserved himself through wit.

sentences.zh: 好縱橫大言，時時讜議，能寤移人主。

translations.literal: He loved grand, sweeping rhetoric and from time to time offered candid remonstrance, capable of awakening and shifting his lord's mind.
translations.idiomatic: He loved bold, sweeping rhetoric and from time to time offered candid remonstrance, capable of awakening and changing his sovereign's mind.

sentences.zh: 然常持黃老鬼神說，故為人所譏切。

translations.literal: Yet he constantly adhered to Yellow Emperor, Laozi, and spirit doctrines, and so was sharply criticized by others.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he constantly invoked the teachings of the Yellow Emperor, Laozi, and the realm of spirits, and so drew sharp criticism.

sentences.zh: 初，肅宗重陰陽巫祝，擢王璵執政，大抵興造工役，輒牽禁忌俗說。

translations.literal: Initially, Emperor Suzong valued yin-yang diviners and shamans and promoted Wang Yu to power; whenever construction or public works were undertaken, taboos and popular superstitions were invoked.
translations.idiomatic: At first Emperor Suzong valued yin-yang diviners and shamans and promoted Wang Yu to power; whenever construction or public works were undertaken, taboos and popular superstitions were invoked.

sentences.zh: 而黎幹以左道位京兆尹，嘗使禁工駢珠刺繡為乘輿服，舉焚之以為禳禬。

translations.literal: Li Gan, by heterodox arts, held the post of Governor of Jingzhao; he once had palace artisans embroider pearl-studded imperial garments and burned them all as exorcistic offering.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gan, through heterodox arts, held the post of Governor of Jingzhao; he once had palace artisans embroider pearl-studded imperial garments and burned them all as exorcistic offerings.

sentences.zh: 德宗素不為然，及嗣位，罷內道場，除巫祝。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong had never approved of such things; once he succeeded to the throne he abolished the inner ordination halls and dismissed shamans.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong had never approved of such things; once he succeeded to the throne he abolished the inner ordination halls and dismissed the shamans.

sentences.zh: 代宗將葬，帝號送承天門，而轀車行不中道，問其故，有司曰：「陛下本命在午，故避之。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong was about to be buried, the Emperor wailed in escort at Chengtian Gate; yet the funeral carriage did not travel the middle of the road. Asked why, the responsible officials said: "Your Majesty's natal sign is in the Wu hour, so the route was avoided."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daizong was about to be buried, the Emperor wailed in escort at Chengtian Gate, yet the funeral carriage did not travel the middle of the road. Asked why, the responsible officials said: "Your Majesty's natal sign falls in the Wu hour, so the route was avoided.

sentences.zh: 帝泣曰：「安有枉靈駕以謀身利？」

translations.literal: The Emperor wept and said: "How could one bend the spirit carriage to plot personal advantage?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wept and said: "How could one bend the imperial hearse to seek personal advantage?"

sentences.zh: 命直午而行。

translations.literal: He ordered that it proceed directly through the Wu hour's position.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the procession to proceed straight through the Wu hour's position.

sentences.zh: 又宣政廊壞，太卜言：「孟冬魁岡，不可營繕。」

translations.literal: Also, the Xuanzheng corridor collapsed; the grand diviner said: "In early winter, Kui Gang forbids repairs."
translations.idiomatic: Also, the Xuanzheng corridor collapsed; the grand diviner said: "In early winter, under the Kui Gang taboo, repairs are forbidden.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「《春秋》『啟塞從時』，何魁岡為？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The Spring and Autumn Annals says, 'Open and close according to the season'—what has Kui Gang to do with it?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "The Spring and Autumn Annals says, 'Open and close according to the season'—what has Kui Gang to do with it?"

sentences.zh: 亟詔葺之。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered it rebuilt.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered it repaired.

sentences.zh: 及桑道茂城奉天事驗，始尚時日拘忌，因進用泌，泌亦自有所建明。

translations.literal: When Sang Daomao's prophecy about fortifying Fengtian was verified, the Emperor began to honor calendar and day taboos and accordingly advanced Bi; Bi also had proposals of his own to put forward.
translations.idiomatic: When Sang Daomao's prophecy about fortifying Fengtian was fulfilled, the Emperor began to observe calendar and day taboos and accordingly promoted Bi; Bi also had proposals of his own to advance.

sentences.zh: 獨柳玭稱，兩京復，泌謀居多，其功乃大於魯連、范蠡云。

translations.literal: Only Liu Bin praised him: when the two capitals were recovered, Bi's stratagems predominated—his achievement, it was said, surpassed even those of Lu Zhonglian and Fan Li.
translations.idiomatic: Only Liu Bin praised him, saying that when the two capitals were recovered Bi's stratagems had predominated and his achievement surpassed even those of Lu Zhonglian and Fan Li.

sentences.zh: 子 繁子繁。

translations.literal: Son: Fan. Fan.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Fan.

sentences.zh: 繁少才警，無行。

translations.literal: Fan was quick-witted from youth but lacked moral conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was clever from boyhood but utterly without moral restraint.

sentences.zh: 泌始起陽城官諸朝，故城重德泌而親厚於繁。

translations.literal: When Bi first raised Yang Cheng to office at court, Cheng revered Bi's virtue and grew close to Fan.
translations.idiomatic: When Bi first raised Yang Cheng to office at court, Cheng revered Bi's virtue and grew intimate with Fan.

sentences.zh: 及疏裴延齡，既具槁，以繁可信，夜使繁書。

translations.literal: When Cheng drafted his memorial denouncing Pei Yanling, once the draft was complete he thought Fan trustworthy and had Fan copy it by night.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng drafted his memorial denouncing Pei Yanling, once the draft was complete he considered Fan trustworthy and had him copy it by night.

sentences.zh: 已封，盡能誦憶，乃錄以示延齡。

translations.literal: After it was sealed, Fan could recite it all from memory and recorded it to show Yanling.
translations.idiomatic: After it was sealed, Fan memorized the entire text and wrote it down to show Yanling.

sentences.zh: 明日，延齡白帝曰：「城以疏示於朝。」

translations.literal: The next day Yanling reported to the Emperor: "Cheng has shown his memorial to the court."
translations.idiomatic: The next day Yanling reported to the Emperor: "Cheng has already shown his memorial to the court.

sentences.zh: 即擿其條以自訴解。

translations.literal: He immediately plucked out each clause to plead his own defense.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately took up each charge in turn to plead his own defense.

sentences.zh: 城奏入，帝怒，遂不省。

translations.literal: When Cheng's memorial was submitted, the Emperor grew angry and would not examine it.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng's memorial was submitted, the Emperor grew angry and refused even to read it.

sentences.zh: 泌與梁肅善，故繁師事肅。

translations.literal: Bi was on good terms with Liang Su, so Fan took Su as his teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Bi was on good terms with Liang Su, so Fan took Su as his master.

sentences.zh: 及卒，烝其室，士議喧醜，由是擯棄積年。

translations.literal: When Su died, Fan seduced his widow; scholarly opinion erupted in scandal, and for this he was cast aside for many years.
translations.idiomatic: When Su died, Fan took his widow; scholarly opinion erupted in outrage, and for this he was cast aside for many years.

sentences.zh: 後為太常博士，權德輿為卿，奏斥之，改河南府士曹參軍。

translations.literal: Later he served as Academician Explanator of the Grand Temple; when Quan Deyu became Minister, he memorialized to dismiss Fan, who was reassigned as Army Staff Officer of Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as Academician Explanator of the Grand Temple; when Quan Deyu became Minister of Rites, he memorialized to have Fan dismissed, and Fan was reassigned as Army Staff Officer of Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 累遷隋州刺史，罷歸，不得調。

translations.literal: After successive promotions to Prefect of Suizhou, he was dismissed and returned home, unable to secure reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: After successive promotions he became Prefect of Suizhou; dismissed and sent home, he could obtain no further appointment.

sentences.zh: 敬宗誕日，詔與兵部侍郎丁公著、太常少卿陸亙入殿中，抗老、佛誦論。

translations.literal: On Emperor Jingzong's birthday, an edict summoned him with Vice Minister of War Ding Gongzhu and Vice Minister of the Grand Temple Lu Gen into the hall to debate Daoism and Buddhism in turn.
translations.idiomatic: On Emperor Jingzong's birthday, an edict summoned him together with Vice Minister of War Ding Gongzhu and Vice Minister of the Grand Temple Lu Gen into the hall to debate alternately on Daoism and Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 改大理少卿、弘文館學士。

translations.literal: He was made Vice Minister of Justice and Academic of the Hongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Minister of Justice and Academic of the Hongwen Institute.

sentences.zh: 諫官御史交章彈治，乃出為亳州刺史。

translations.literal: Censorial remonstrators submitted memorial after memorial calling for his punishment, and he was dispatched as Prefect of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating officials and censors submitted memorial after memorial calling for his punishment, and he was dispatched as Prefect of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 州有劇賊，剽室廬、略財貲為患，它刺史不能禽，繁有機略，悉知賊巢藪所在，一旦出兵捕斬之。

translations.literal: The prefecture had fierce bandits who plundered houses and looted goods; other prefects could not capture them. Fan had stratagem and knew all their lairs; one day he led troops out and captured and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture had fierce bandits who raided homes and looted goods; other prefects could not capture them. Fan was resourceful and knew every bandit lair; one day he led troops out and captured and executed them.

sentences.zh: 議者責繁不先啟觀察府，為擅興。

translations.literal: Critics blamed Fan for not first reporting to the observation commissioner—charging him with unauthorized action.
translations.idiomatic: Critics blamed Fan for not first informing the observation commissioner, charging him with unauthorized mobilization.

sentences.zh: 詔御史舒元輿按之，元輿與繁素隙，盡翻其獄，以為濫殺不辜，有詔賜死，京兆人皆冤之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Censor Shu Yuanyu to investigate; Yuanyu and Fan had long been at odds, and he overturned the entire case, deeming it indiscriminate slaughter of the innocent. An edict ordered Fan's death by grace; the people of Jingzhao all considered it a wrongful verdict.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Censor Shu Yuanyu to investigate; Yuanyu and Fan had long been at odds, and he overturned the entire case, deeming it indiscriminate slaughter of the innocent. An edict ordered Fan's death by imperial grace, and the people of the capital all considered it a wrongful verdict.

sentences.zh: 繁下獄，知且死，恐先人功業泯滅，從吏求廢紙，筆握著家傳十篇，傳於世。

translations.literal: Imprisoned, knowing he would soon die, Fan feared his forebear's achievements would perish; he begged scrap paper from the jailers and, brush in hand, wrote ten chapters of a family biography that were handed down to the world.
translations.idiomatic: Imprisoned and knowing he would soon die, Fan feared his forebear's achievements would be lost; he begged scrap paper from the jailers and, brush in hand, wrote ten chapters of a family biography that were handed down to posterity.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：泌之為人也，異哉！

translations.literal: The encomium says: As a man, Bi was extraordinary indeed!
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Bi was an extraordinary man indeed!

sentences.zh: 其謀事近忠，其輕去近高，其自全近智，卒而建上宰，近立功立名者。

translations.literal: In counsel he approached loyalty; in lightly letting go of office he approached loftiness; in preserving himself he approached wisdom—and in the end he reached the chancellorship, approaching one who establishes merit and fame.
translations.idiomatic: In stratagem he approached loyalty; in readily leaving office he approached high-mindedness; in preserving himself he approached wisdom—and in the end he rose to Grand Chancellor, approaching the ranks of those who establish merit and make a name.

sentences.zh: 觀肅宗披榛莽，立朝廷，單言暫謀有所寤合，皆付以政。

translations.literal: Consider how Emperor Suzong cleared through thorns and brambles to establish the court: whenever a single word or brief stratagem met his understanding, he entrusted Bi with governance.
translations.idiomatic: Consider how Emperor Suzong cut through thorns and brambles to establish the court: whenever a single remark or brief stratagem struck home, he entrusted Bi with governance.

sentences.zh: 當此時，泌於獻納為不少，又佐代宗收兩京，獨不見錄，寧二主不以宰相器之邪？

translations.literal: At that time Bi's memorials and remonstrance were no small contribution; he also aided Daizong in recovering the two capitals—yet alone he received no formal record. Surely both emperors did not regard him as material for chancellor?
translations.idiomatic: At that time Bi's remonstrance and memorials were no small contribution, and he also aided Daizong in recovering the two capitals—yet he alone received no formal recognition. Surely both emperors did not regard him as chancellor material?

sentences.zh: 德宗晚好鬼神事，乃獲用，蓋以怪自置而為之助也。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong in his later years favored spirit affairs, and only then was Bi employed—likely because he placed himself in the realm of the uncanny and thereby assisted in that path.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong in his later years favored affairs of spirits and omens, and only then was Bi employed—likely because he had placed himself in that uncanny realm and thereby served as an instrument of it.

sentences.zh: 繁為家傳，言泌本居鬼谷，而史臣謬言好鬼道，以自解釋。

translations.literal: In his family biography Fan wrote that Bi originally dwelt at Ghost Valley, while the historians wrongly say he favored the Way of ghosts—an explanation for himself.
translations.idiomatic: In his family biography Fan wrote that Bi originally dwelt at Ghost Valley, while the historians wrongly say he favored the Way of ghosts—an explanation offered on his own behalf.

sentences.zh: 既又著泌數與靈仙接，言舉不經，則知當時議者切而不與，有為而然。

translations.literal: He also recorded that Bi frequently consorted with immortals—language altogether unorthodox—showing that contemporary critics were sharp and did not agree; there was reason for their stance.
translations.idiomatic: He also recorded that Bi frequently consorted with immortals—language altogether unorthodox—showing that contemporary critics were sharp in their judgment and did not agree; they had grounds for their objections.

sentences.zh: 繁言多浮侈，不可信，掇其近實者著於傳。

translations.literal: Fan's words are mostly extravagant and not to be trusted; only what approaches truth has been selected for this biography.
translations.idiomatic: Fan's words are mostly extravagant and not to be trusted; only what approaches truth has been selected for this biography.

sentences.zh: 至勸帝先事范陽，明太子無罪，亦不可誣也。

translations.literal: As for advising the emperor to strike Fan Yang first and making clear the Heir Apparent's innocence—these cannot be falsified either.
translations.idiomatic: As for his counsel that the emperor strike Fan Yang first and his demonstration that the Heir Apparent was innocent—these cannot be falsified either.
